01Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

100X Postgres Scaling at Figma

Figma ke users 200% badhe — aur unka Postgres database 100x bada ho gaya. Ek database se kaam nahi chal raha tha. Unhone 3 steps me scale kiya: pehle bada server, phir alag-alag databases, phir data ko tukdon me baantna. Ye real-world scaling ki kahani hai.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — upar wali cheez ko ek nazar me samjho. Image file ke andar embedded hai, isliye bina internet ke bhi dikhegi.

1. Figma ki problem kya thi? — godown wali kahani

Socho tumhara godown (database) bhar gaya hai — saaman (data) itna badh gaya ki jagah hi nahi bachi. Pehle tum bada godown lete ho (vertical scaling). Phir bhi kam pad jaye to alag-alag godown karte ho — ek me kapde, ek me electronics (vertical partitioning). Phir bhi kam pad jaye to har godown ko tukdon me baant dete ho — kapdon ka godown 5 hisson me (horizontal partitioning). Figma ne bhi yahi 3 steps liye — ek ke baad ek, jab zaroorat padi.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Scaling ek journey hai — pehle vertical (bada server), phir vertical partitioning (alag DBs), phir horizontal partitioning (sharding). Har step tab lo jab pichhla kam pad jaye.

2. Figma ke 3 scaling steps

Har step ek problem solve karta hai — tabs me samjho.

Step 1: Vertical Scaling + Replication

Pehle Figma ne sabse bada server liya — Amazon RDS ko r5.12xlarge se r5.24xlarge pe upgrade kiya (sabse bada available). Saath me read replicas banaye — padhne wale queries replicas pe jayein, likhne wale main DB pe. Aur PgBouncer lagaya — connection pooler, taaki hazaaron connections DB ko mar na dein. Example: 3 million users ke reads replicas pe bat gaye — main DB ka load kam ho gaya. Limit: server kitna bhi bada lo, ek limit hoti hai — aur single point of failure bhi rehta hai.

Sahi tareeka: Pehle vertical scaling karo — sabse aasan step hai.
Galat tareeka: Sirf vertical scaling pe depend karna — ek limit ke baad aur bada server nahi milega.

Step 2: Vertical Partitioning

Jab ek DB bhi kam pad gaya to Figma ne high-traffic tables ko alag databases me daal diya — 'Figma Files' aur 'Organizations' jaise bade tables apne alag DB me gaye. Example: pehle sab kuch ek DB me tha — ab files ka DB alag, organizations ka alag, baaki ka alag. Har DB ke liye alag PgBouncer lagaya — connections manage karne ke liye. Fayda: ek table ka load dusre ko affect nahi karta — isolation mil gaya. Limit: kuch tables itne bade ho gaye ki ek DB me bhi nahi sama rahe the.

Sahi tareeka: Bade tables ko alag DB me daalna — isolation milta hai.
Galat tareeka: Har table ko alag DB me daal dena — joins mushkil ho jayenge.

Step 3: Horizontal Partitioning (Sharding)

Kuch tables kai terabytes aur billions of rows ke ho gaye — Postgres Vacuum (cleanup) problem ban gaya aur RDS ki max IOPS limit cross ho gayi. Solution: horizontal partitioning — ek bade table ko kai physical databases me baant diya (sharding). Example: files table ko user ID ke hisaab se 10 databases me baanta — user 1-1000 DB1 pe, 1001-2000 DB2 pe. DBProxy banaya — ek service jo routing aur query execution sambhalti hai (client ko pata nahi chalta data kahan hai). Note: sharding sabse mushkil step hai — cross-shard queries aur transactions mushkil ho jate hain.

Sahi tareeka: Jab ek table terabytes ka ho jaye to sharding karo.
Galat tareeka: Pehle din se sharding karna — bahut complexity, bina zaroorat ke mat karo.

PgBouncer aur DBProxy — do helpers

PgBouncer ek connection pooler hai — hazaaron app connections ko kuch DB connections me badal deta hai. Bina iske har user ka connection DB ko overload kar dega. DBProxy Figma ki khud ki service hai — sharding ke baad client ko pata nahi chalta data kis DB me hai; DBProxy query ko sahi shard pe bhejta hai aur results jod ke deta hai. Example: tum user 1500 ka file maango — DBProxy samajh jata hai wo DB2 pe hai, wahan se la ke deta hai. Note: ye dono Figma ke scaling ke unsung heroes hain.

Sahi tareeka: Connection pooling (PgBouncer) pehle din se lagana.
Galat tareeka: Har connection ko seedha DB pe bhejna — DB mar jayega.

3. Scaling journey — ek table me

Har step kab lena hai, ye samjho — jaldi karna bhi galat hai, der karna bhi.

CheezDetail (Hinglish me)
Step 1: VerticalBada server + read replicas + PgBouncer. Kab: shuruaat me, sabse aasan.
Step 2: Vertical PartitioningBade tables alag DB me. Kab: jab ek DB me sab kuch slow ho jaye.
Step 3: Horizontal (Sharding)Table ko kai DBs me baanto + DBProxy. Kab: jab table terabytes ka ho jaye.
Read ReplicasReads ko replicas pe bhejo — main DB sirf writes ke liye.
PgBouncerConnection pooling — hazaaron connections ko manage karo.
DBProxySharding ke baad routing — client ko pata na chale data kahan hai.
# Figma scaling journey — timeline
#
# 2018: 1 Postgres (RDS r5.12xlarge)
#   Users badhe -> 200% growth
#
# Step 1: Vertical scaling
#   -> r5.24xlarge (sabse bada)
#   -> Read replicas + PgBouncer
#
# Step 2: Vertical partitioning
#   -> 'Figma Files' alag DB me
#   -> 'Organizations' alag DB me
#
# Step 3: Horizontal partitioning
#   -> Tables kai TB ke — sharding karo
#   -> DBProxy banaya (routing + queries)
#
# Result: 100X growth handle ho gaya!

Dhyan do: Figma ne sharding sabse aakhir me kiya — jab zaroorat padi. Pehle aasan steps liye. Scaling me order matter karta hai.

4. Try karo — Figma scaling simulator

Figma ka database badh raha hai — har step pe dekho kya hota hai.

Step 1 — Vertical scaling

  • Users: 3 million, DB: r5.12xlarge (full!)
  • Action: r5.24xlarge pe upgrade + 3 read replicas
  • PgBouncer lagaya — connections pool ho gaye
  • Result: load kam hua — lekin ek limit hai, aage kya?

Step 2 — Vertical partitioning

  • 'Figma Files' table bahut bada ho gaya
  • Action: Files ko alag DB me, Organizations ko alag DB me
  • Har DB ka alag PgBouncer
  • Result: ek table ka load dusre ko affect nahi karta!

Step 3 — Sharding

  • Files table: kai TB, billions of rows!
  • Problem: Vacuum slow, IOPS limit cross
  • Action: table ko 10 shards me baanta (user ID se)
  • DBProxy banaya — routing sambhalta hai
  • Result: 100X growth handle ho gaya!

Bina scaling ke kya hota

  • Users badhe, DB wahi purana
  • Connections: DB overload — queries slow
  • Result: Figma slow ho jata, users chale jate
  • Lesson: scaling pehle se plan karo, crisis me nahi!

5. Kab kya use karein

Option / SituationKab aur kyun
Shuruaat meVertical scaling + read replicas — sabse aasan.
Ek table bahut bada hoVertical partitioning — use alag DB me daalo.
Table terabytes ka hoHorizontal partitioning (sharding) + DBProxy.
Connections zyada honPgBouncer — connection pooling lagao.
Reads zyada honRead replicas — main DB sirf writes ke liye.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  • Pehle din se sharding karna — bahut complexity, bina zaroorat ke mat karo.
  • Sirf vertical scaling pe depend karna — ek limit ke baad aur bada server nahi milega.
  • Connection pooling na lagana — hazaaron connections DB ko mar denge.
  • Scaling ko crisis me karna — pehle se plan karo, metrics dekho.

7. Interview corner

Q: Figma ne Postgres ko 100x kaise scale kiya?

3 steps me: pehle vertical scaling (sabse bada RDS + read replicas + PgBouncer), phir vertical partitioning (bade tables alag DB me), phir horizontal partitioning (sharding + DBProxy). Har step tab liya jab pichhla kam pad gaya.

Q: Vertical aur Horizontal scaling me kya farak hai?

Vertical matlab ek hi server ko bada karna (zyada CPU/RAM) — aasan hai lekin ek limit hoti hai. Horizontal matlab kai servers me baantna (sharding) — mushkil hai lekin unlimited scale hota hai. Figma ne dono use kiye — pehle vertical, phir horizontal.

Q: PgBouncer kya hai aur kyun zaroori hai?

PgBouncer ek connection pooler hai — hazaaron app connections ko kuch DB connections me badal deta hai. Bina iske har user ka connection DB ko overload kar dega. Scaling me connection pooling pehle din se lagani chahiye.

8. Quick check

Q1. Figma ne sabse pehle kaunsa scaling step liya?

  • Sharding
  • Vertical scaling (bada server + replicas)
  • Vertical partitioning

Q2. Jab ek table kai terabytes ka ho jaye to kya karte hain?

  • Aur bada server lete hain
  • Horizontal partitioning (sharding)
  • Table delete kar dete hain

02Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

API of APIs - App Integrations

Har app dusri apps se judna chahti hai — Slack me Google Drive, Notion me Figma, Zapier me sab kuch. Ye integrations kaise bante hain? Jawab hai: API of APIs — ek aisi API jo dusri APIs ko jodti hai. Is page me app integrations ka architecture samjho.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — upar wali cheez ko ek nazar me samjho. Image file ke andar embedded hai, isliye bina internet ke bhi dikhegi.

1. API of APIs kya hai? — adapter wali kahani

Tumhare paas 5 alag chargers hain — ek phone ka, ek laptop ka, ek tablet ka. Har baar alag charger dhoondhna mushkil hai. API of APIs ek universal adapter hai — ek hi charger se sab charge ho jata hai. Jaise har device ka alag plug hota hai, waise hi har app ki alag API hoti hai — Slack ki alag, Drive ki alag, Notion ki alag. Ek integration platform (jaise Zapier ya Merge) in sab ke upar ek single API banata hai — tum ek hi tareeke se sabse baat karo.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: API of APIs = ek unified API jo kai alag APIs ko jodti hai. Developer ko har app ki alag API seekhne ki zaroorat nahi — ek hi seekho, sabse baat karo.

2. App integrations kaise kaam karte hain

Har concept ek layer hai — tabs me samjho.

Problem — har app ki alag API

Har app ki API alag hoti hai — alag auth (OAuth), alag endpoints, alag data format, alag rate limits. Example: Slack se message bhejna alag tareeke se, Google Drive se file lena alag tareeke se, Notion se page banana alag tareeke se. Ek app ko 10 apps se judna ho to 10 alag integrations likhne padte hain — har ek ka auth, error handling, aur data mapping alag. Problem: ye bahut time aur maintenance mangta hai — ek app ki API badle to tumhara integration toot jayega.

Sahi tareeka: Har integration ko alag se likhna — time aur maintenance dono zyada.
Galat tareeka: Ye sochna ki saari APIs ek jaisi hain — har ek alag hoti hai.

Solution — Unified API

Ek unified API (jaise Merge, Nango, ya Zapier) saari apps ke upar ek layer banati hai — tum ek hi API se sabse baat karo. Example: POST /unified/messages — peeche ye Slack, Teams ya Discord — kisi ko bhi bhej sakta hai, tumhe farak nahi padta. Unified API har app ki alag-alag cheezon ko normalize karti hai — alag formats ko ek format me badal deti hai. Fayda: ek integration likho, 10 apps se jud jao.

Sahi tareeka: Unified API use karna — ek integration, kai apps.
Galat tareeka: Har app ke liye alag integration likhna — maintenance nightmare.

OAuth — har app se permission

Integration ke liye har app se permission leni padti hai — OAuth se. User 'Connect Slack' dabata hai → Slack pe login karta hai → permission deta hai → tumhe token milta hai. Example: tum Notion ko Figma se jodte ho — Notion Figma se OAuth token mangta hai, user allow karta hai, phir Notion Figma ki API bula sakta hai. Note: har app ka OAuth flow alag hota hai — unified API ye bhi sambhal leti hai (ek hi OAuth flow sab ke liye). Problem: token expire ho jaye to refresh karna padta hai — har app ka alag rule hai.

Sahi tareeka: OAuth se permission lena — user ki marzi se.
Galat tareeka: User ka password store karna — kabhi mat karo, OAuth use karo.

Webhooks aur Sync

Integration sirf 'data lena' nahi hai — sync bhi karna padta hai. Jab Slack me kuch badle to tumhari app ko pata kaise chalega? Webhooks se — har app event hone pe tumhe batati hai. Example: Google Drive me nayi file aaye to webhook aata hai — tumhari app turant sync kar leti hai. Note: har app ke webhooks alag hote hain — unified API unhe bhi normalize karti hai (ek hi format me events). Problem: webhook miss ho jaye to data out-of-sync ho jata hai — isliye periodic sync bhi chahiye.

Sahi tareeka: Webhooks + periodic sync — dono se data updated rahe.
Galat tareeka: Sirf webhooks pe depend karna — miss ho jaye to sync toot jayega.

3. Integration ka poora flow

User 'Connect' dabaye se leke data sync hone tak — poora flow.

CheezDetail (Hinglish me)
1. User Connect dabata haiTumhari app me 'Connect Slack' button — OAuth flow shuru.
2. OAuth permissionUser Slack pe login karke permission deta hai — token milta hai.
3. Token store karoToken ko encrypted store karo — kabhi plain text me nahi.
4. Unified API call karoPOST /unified/messages — peeche Slack ya Teams, tumhe farak nahi.
5. Webhook se updatesSlack me kuch badle to webhook aata hai — tumhari app sync karti hai.
6. Periodic syncHar ghante full sync — webhook miss ho to bhi data sahi rahe.
# Unified API — ek call, kai apps
# Tum likhte ho:
#   POST /unified/messages
#   { "channel": "general", "text": "Hello!" }
#
# Unified API peeche karti hai:
#   Slack:    POST /chat.postMessage
#   Teams:    POST /teams/{id}/channels/{id}/messages
#   Discord:  POST /channels/{id}/messages
#
# Tumhe sirf ek API seekhni hai —
# peeche 3 alag APIs ko unified API sambhalti hai!

Unified API ka asli kaam normalization hai — alag-alag APIs ke alag formats ko ek format me badalna.

4. Try karo — App integration simulator

Ek app ko 3 apps se jodo — pehle seedha, phir unified API se.

Seedha integration (bina unified API)

  • Slack integration likho — auth, endpoints, format (2 hafte)
  • Teams integration likho — alag auth, alag format (2 hafte)
  • Discord integration likho — phir se alag (2 hafte)
  • Total: 6 hafte, 3 alag codebases — aur har app ki API badle to fix karo!
  • Result: maintenance nightmare!

Unified API se

  • Unified API seekho — ek hi format (2 din)
  • POST /unified/messages — Slack, Teams, Discord — sabko jata hai!
  • Nayi app judni ho to: unified API pehle se support karti hai
  • Total: 2 din me 3 apps se jud gaye!
  • Result: 20x fast!

OAuth flow

  • User: 'Connect Slack' dabata hai
  • Slack pe login → permission deta hai
  • Token milta hai — encrypted store karo
  • Ab tumhari app Slack ki API bula sakti hai
  • Token expire ho to: refresh token se naya banao

5. Kab kya use karein

Option / SituationKab aur kyun
1-2 apps se judna hoSeedha integration — simple hai, kaafi hai.
10+ apps se judna hoUnified API — ek integration, sabse jud jao.
User ki permission chahiyeOAuth — password kabhi mat maango.
Real-time sync chahiyeWebhooks + periodic sync — dono lagao.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  • Har app ke liye alag integration likhna — unified API se time bachao.
  • User ka password store karna — OAuth use karo, kabhi password mat lo.
  • Sirf webhooks pe depend karna — miss ho jaye to sync toot jayega.
  • Token ko plain text me store karna — encrypted rakho.

7. Interview corner

Q: API of APIs kya hai?

Ek unified API jo kai alag APIs ko jodti hai — developer ek hi API se kai apps se baat kar sakta hai. Jaise Merge ya Zapier — ek integration se Slack, Teams, Discord sabse jud jao. Har app ki alag API seekhne ki zaroorat nahi.

Q: App integrations me OAuth kyun use karte hain?

Taaki user apna password diye bina permission de sake. User app pe login karke allow karta hai, tumhe token milta hai — password tumhare paas kabhi nahi aata. Token expire bhi hota hai aur revoke bhi ho sakta hai.

Q: Webhooks aur periodic sync dono kyun chahiye?

Webhooks real-time updates dete hain, lekin miss ho sakte hain (server down ho to). Periodic sync (har ghante full check) se data hamesha sahi rehta hai — webhook miss ho bhi jaye to sync se theek ho jayega.

8. Quick check

Q1. 10 apps se judna ho to best tareeka kaunsa hai?

  • Har app ke liye alag integration likho
  • Unified API use karo — ek integration, sabse jud jao
  • Kisi se mat judo

Q2. User se permission lene ka sahi tareeka kaunsa hai?

  • Password maango
  • OAuth — user login karke allow kare
  • Bina permission ke data lo
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/api-of-apis-app-integrations.md

03Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

Fixing Bugs Automatically at Meta Scale

Meta (Facebook) pe har roz lakhon lines code likha jata hai — aur bugs bhi lakhon me hote hain. Insaan se sab fix karna impossible hai. Isliye Meta ne automatic bug fixing banaya — AI aur tools khud bugs dhoondhte hain, fix karte hain, aur test karte hain. Ye kahani hai ki scale pe bugs kaise fix hote hain.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — upar wali cheez ko ek nazar me samjho. Image file ke andar embedded hai, isliye bina internet ke bhi dikhegi.

1. Automatic bug fixing kya hai? — factory wali kahani

Ek car factory me insaan har car ko check karta tha — slow aur galti hoti thi. Phir machines aa gayi — har car ko scan karo, defect mile to turant fix karo, phir dobara check karo. Meta ka bug fixing bhi wahi hai: pehle insaan bugs dhoondhta tha, ab tools (static analysis, AI) khud dhoondhte hain, fix suggest karte hain, aur test karke confirm karte hain. Insaan sirf approve karta hai — jaise factory me supervisor final check karta hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Scale pe manual bug fixing impossible hai — automation zaroori hai. Tools dhoondhte hain, fix karte hain, test karte hain; insaan approve karta hai.

2. Meta kaise bugs fix karta hai — step by step

Har step ek tool ya process hai — tabs me samjho.

Step 1: Bugs dhoondhna — Static Analysis

Code likhte hi static analysis tools (jaise Infer, SapFix) code ko bina chalaye check karte hain — null pointer, memory leak, race condition jaise bugs pakadte hain. Example: tumne ek function likha jo null return kar sakta hai — Infer turant batata hai 'yahan null dereference ho sakta hai'. Note: static analysis code ko chalaye bina bugs dhoondhta hai — isliye fast hai aur har commit pe chal sakta hai. Tools: Infer (Meta ka open-source tool), ESLint, SonarQube.

Sahi tareeka: Har commit pe static analysis chalana — bugs pehle hi pakdo.
Galat tareeka: Static analysis ko ignore karna — bugs production me milenge.

Step 2: Fix suggest karna — AI aur Patterns

Bug milne ke baad tool fix suggest karta hai — pehle ke fixes ke patterns se seekh ke. Example: null dereference mila to tool suggest karta hai 'yahan null check add karo' — aur code bhi likh ke deta hai. AI: Meta ke tools past fixes se seekhte hain — kis tarah ke bug ka kis tarah ka fix hota hai. Note: fix hamesha sahi nahi hota — isliye insaan review karta hai. Lekin 80% fixes sahi hote hain — bahut time bachta hai.

Sahi tareeka: Tool ke suggested fix ko review karke accept karna.
Galat tareeka: Auto-fix ko bina dekhe accept karna — galat fix bhi ho sakta hai.

Step 3: Test karna — Automatic Verification

Fix lagne ke baad tests automatic chalte hain — kya fix ne bug theek kiya? Kya kuch aur toota? Example: fix ke baad unit tests, integration tests aur regression tests chalte hain — sab pass ho to fix aage badhta hai. Note: Meta pe har fix ke liye tests zaroori hain — bina tests ke fix merge nahi hota. Tools: CI/CD pipeline, automated test suites.

Sahi tareeka: Har fix ke saath tests chalana — bina test ke merge mat karo.
Galat tareeka: Fix karke test na karna — fix se naya bug aa sakta hai.

Step 4: Human Review aur Deploy

Aakhir me insaan review karta hai — fix sahi hai? Code style theek hai? Phir deploy hota hai — pehle chhote group pe (canary), phir sab pe. Example: auto-fix ne 100 bugs fix kiye — insaan ne 95 approve kiye, 5 reject kiye (galat fix the). Note: automation insaan ki jagah nahi leta — insaan ka kaam approve karna aur edge cases dekhna hai. Lesson: best system hai human + AI — AI fast hai, insaan smart hai.

Sahi tareeka: Auto-fix ko hamesha human review se guzarna.
Galat tareeka: Automation pe poora bharosa karke review skip karna.

3. Automatic bug fixing ka pipeline

Bug aane se leke fix deploy hone tak — poora flow.

CheezDetail (Hinglish me)
1. Code likha gayaDeveloper code commit karta hai.
2. Static analysisInfer jaise tools bugs dhoondhte hain — bina code chalaye.
3. Fix suggestTool past patterns se fix likh ke deta hai.
4. Tests chalte hainFix ne bug theek kiya? Kuch aur toota to nahi?
5. Human reviewInsaan fix ko check karta hai — approve ya reject.
6. DeployCanary pe pehle, phir sab pe — gradual rollout.
# Meta ka bug fixing pipeline (conceptual)
#
# Developer commits code
#   -> Infer (static analysis) runs
#   -> Bug found: null dereference at line 42!
#   -> SapFix suggests: add null check
#   -> Fix applied automatically
#   -> Tests run: all pass ✓
#   -> Human reviews: approves ✓
#   -> Deployed via canary (5% -> 100%)
#
# Result: bug fix hua bina developer ko
# kuch kiye — sirf approve karna pada!

Infer Meta ka open-source static analysis tool hai — tum bhi use kar sakte ho apne projects me. SapFix uska auto-fix wala hissa hai.

4. Try karo — Automatic bug fixing simulator

Ek bug aaya — dekho Meta ka system use kaise fix karta hai.

Bug aaya

  • Developer ne code commit kiya
  • Infer (static analysis) chala — bug mila!
  • Bug: null dereference, line 42 — 'user' null ho sakta hai
  • Result: bug production jaane se pehle pakda gaya!

Fix suggest hua

  • SapFix ne past fixes dekhe — is bug ka fix pata hai
  • Suggested fix: 'if (user == null) return;' add karo
  • Fix automatic lag gaya — developer ko kuch nahi karna pada
  • Result: fix ready hai — ab test aur review baki hai.

Tests chale

  • Unit tests: PASS ✓
  • Integration tests: PASS ✓
  • Regression tests: PASS ✓ — kuch aur nahi toota
  • Result: fix verified — ab human review pe jao.

Human review + Deploy

  • Insaan ne fix dekha — sahi hai, approve!
  • Deploy: canary 5% users pe — sab theek
  • Deploy: 100% users pe — bug fix ho gaya!
  • Result: bug fix hua — developer ka time bacha!

5. Kab kya use karein

Option / SituationKab aur kyun
Bugs jaldi pakadne honStatic analysis — har commit pe chalao.
Fix suggest karna hoAI/pattern-based tools — SapFix jaisa.
Fix verify karna hoAutomated tests — bina test ke merge mat karo.
Final decision hoHuman review — automation ko approve karo, blind trust mat karo.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  • Auto-fix ko bina review ke accept karna — galat fix bhi ho sakta hai.
  • Static analysis ko ignore karna — bugs production me milenge.
  • Fix karke test na karna — fix se naya bug aa sakta hai.
  • Ye samajhna ki automation insaan ki jagah le lega — human review hamesha zaroori hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: Meta bugs ko automatically kaise fix karta hai?

4 steps me: static analysis tools (Infer) bugs dhoondhte hain, AI/pattern-based tools (SapFix) fix suggest karte hain, automated tests fix ko verify karte hain, aur insaan review karke approve karta hai. Phir canary deploy hota hai.

Q: Static analysis kya hai?

Code ko bina chalaye check karna — bugs, security issues aur code smells dhoondhna. Tools (Infer, ESLint, SonarQube) code ko padh ke patterns match karte hain. Fast hai aur har commit pe chal sakta hai.

Q: Automatic fixing me human review kyun zaroori hai?

Kyunki auto-fix hamesha sahi nahi hota — 80% sahi hote hain, 20% galat ya incomplete ho sakte hain. Insaan edge cases aur business logic samajhta hai jo tool nahi samajhta. Best system hai human + AI.

8. Quick check

Q1. Meta ka static analysis tool kaunsa hai?

  • ESLint
  • Infer
  • SonarQube

Q2. Auto-fix ke baad sabse important step kaunsa hai?

  • Turant deploy karo
  • Tests + human review
  • Kuch nahi — fix ho gaya
SapFix ke pilot ke numbers (guide se):
  • SapFix Facebook app family ki 6 key apps par use hua — Facebook, Messenger, Instagram, FBLite, Workplace aur Workchat. Har app me tens of millions of lines of code hain.
  • 90-day pilot phase me 57 crashes ke liye 165 patches generate kiye gaye.
  • Fault detect hone se lekar fix human approval ke liye bhejne tak ka median time sirf 69 minutes tha.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/fixing-bugs-automatically-at-meta-scale.md
← PichhlaAPI of APIs - App IntegrationsAgla →How Levelsfyi Scaled to Millions of Users with Google Sheets
04Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

How Levelsfyi Scaled to Millions of Users with Google Sheets

Levels.fyi — salary transparency wali site — lakhon users tak pahunch gayi Google Sheets ko backend bana ke! Koi database nahi, koi fancy infrastructure nahi — sirf Sheets, Forms aur serverless. Ye kahani hai ki 'start simple' kitna powerful ho sakta hai.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — upar wali cheez ko ek nazar me samjho. Image file ke andar embedded hai, isliye bina internet ke bhi dikhegi.

1. Google Sheets se scaling? — thela wali kahani

Socho tumhe chai ka thela lagana hai. Tum pehle din se 5-star restaurant nahi khologe — thela lagao, chai becho, log aayein to thela bada karo, phir dukaan, phir restaurant. Levels.fyi ne bhi wahi kiya: pehle Google Forms + Sheets se shuru kiya (thela), users badhe to bhi Sheets hi chalata raha (thela bada kiya), aur jab zaroorat padi tab proper backend banaya (restaurant). Bahut log pehle din se restaurant kholne me time waste karte hain — Levels.fyi ne thele se shuru karke lakhon users tak pahunch gaya.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Start simple, iterate fast. Perfect infrastructure se shuru karna zaroori nahi — pehle users lao, phir scale karo. Sheets se lakhon users handle ho sakte hain, agar design sahi ho.

2. Levels.fyi ne kaise kiya

Har step ek lesson hai — tabs me samjho.

Step 1: Google Forms + Sheets se shuruaat

Levels.fyi ne Google Forms se shuru kiya — log apni salary details form me bharte the, data Google Sheets me jata tha. Website Sheets ko hi backend ki tarah use karti thi — data padh ke dikha deti thi. Example: tum form bharte ho → Sheets me row add hoti hai → website us row ko padh ke salary page pe dikha deti hai. Fayda: zero infrastructure — na database setup, na server, na DevOps. Note: founders ka philosophy tha: 'start simple and iterate' — pehle product banao, infrastructure baad me.

Sahi tareeka: MVP ke liye simple tools use karna — Sheets, Forms, Airtable.
Galat tareeka: Pehle din se perfect infrastructure banana — time waste hoga.

Step 2: Sheets ko database ki tarah use karna

Sheets ko database ki tarah use kiya — har row ek record, har column ek field. Website serverless functions se Sheets API ko call karti thi — data padh ke JSON bana ke frontend ko deti thi. Example: salary page kholo → serverless function Sheets se data laata hai → page pe dikhata hai. Problem: Sheets API ke rate limits hain — zyada requests aayein to slow ho jata hai. Fix: caching — data ko cache karo, har request pe Sheets mat kholo. Note: Sheets database nahi hai — iske limits hain (5 million cells, rate limits) — lekin lakhon users ke liye kaafi tha, caching ke saath.

Sahi tareeka: Sheets ke saamne caching lagana — har request pe API mat bulao.
Galat tareeka: Har request pe Sheets API bulana — rate limit lag jayegi.

Step 3: Serverless + Caching se scale

Website serverless (Vercel/Netlify functions) pe chalti thi — traffic badhe to functions khud scale ho jate hain, server manage nahi karna padta. Caching se Sheets API ke calls kam kiye — data ko CDN/cache me rakha, har kuch minute me refresh kiya. Example: 1 lakh users ek hi salary page dekhein to Sheets ko 1 lakh calls nahi jati — cache se 1 lakh ko jawab mil jata hai. Result: lakhon monthly users — bina kisi database ke! Note: salary data zyada badalta nahi — isliye caching bahut effective thi.

Sahi tareeka: Static/cached data ke liye serverless + CDN use karna.
Galat tareeka: Har request pe database bulana — jab data badalta hi nahi.

Step 4: Jab zaroorat padi, tab proper backend

Aakhir me jab Sheets ki limits aane lagi (data zyada, writes zyada, complex queries), to Levels.fyi ne proper backend banaya — database, API, sab kuch. Example: user submissions badh gayi, real-time features chahiye hue — tab backend banaya. Lesson: backend tab banao jab zaroorat pade — pehle nahi. Bahut startups pehle backend banane me mahine waste karte hain, jabki unhe users hi nahi mile hote. Note: Levels.fyi ka philosophy: 'start simple, iterate' — pehle users lao, phir infrastructure banao.

Sahi tareeka: Backend tab banao jab zaroorat pade — pehle nahi.
Galat tareeka: Pehle din se over-engineering karna — users ke bina backend bekar hai.

3. Levels.fyi ka architecture

Sheets se lakhon users tak — architecture samjho.

CheezDetail (Hinglish me)
Data entryGoogle Forms — users salary bharte hain.
DatabaseGoogle Sheets — har row ek record.
BackendServerless functions — Sheets API se data laate hain.
CachingCDN/cache — har request pe Sheets mat kholo.
FrontendStatic site — fast load, serverless se data.
Scale pointJab Sheets ki limits aayi — tab proper backend banaya.
# Levels.fyi architecture (simplified)
#
# User submits salary
#   -> Google Form
#   -> Google Sheet (row add hoti hai)
#
# User salary page kholta hai
#   -> Serverless function (Vercel)
#   -> Cache check: data hai? Haan -> wapas do
#   -> Cache miss: Sheets API se lo -> cache me bharo
#
# Result: lakhon users, Sheets API ko
# sirf kuch calls per minute — caching ka kamaal!

Caching hi asli hero hai — bina caching ke Sheets API rate limit lag jati aur site slow ho jati. Data zyada badalta nahi tha, isliye caching bahut effective thi.

4. Try karo — Levels.fyi scaling simulator

Ek salary page kholo — dekho Sheets backend kaise handle karta hai.

Pehla user aaya

  • User: salary page kholta hai
  • Serverless function: cache check — EMPTY
  • Sheets API se data laya (1 call) — cache me bhara
  • Response: 800ms — pehli baar slow, lekin theek hai
  • Result: page dikh gaya!

1 lakh users aaye

  • 1 lakh users ne wahi page khola
  • Cache: HIT! — sabko cache se jawab mila
  • Sheets API calls: sirf 1 (cache refresh ke liye)
  • Response: 50ms — bahut fast!
  • Result: caching se 1 lakh users handle ho gaye!

Bina caching ke

  • 1 lakh users — har ek ke liye Sheets API call
  • Sheets API: rate limit lag gayi! (100 req/100 sec)
  • Response: slow + errors — site down!
  • Result: caching ke bina Sheets backend nahi chalega.

Backend migrate karo

  • Data badh gaya — Sheets ki limits aa gayi
  • Action: proper database (Postgres) + API banayi
  • Migration: Sheets se data export karke DB me dala
  • Result: ab aur scale ho sakta hai — lekin sirf tab, jab zaroorat padi!

5. Kab kya use karein

Option / SituationKab aur kyun
MVP banana hoGoogle Sheets/Forms — zero setup, turant shuru karo.
Data zyada badalta nahi hoSheets + caching — bahut scale ho jayega.
Writes zyada honProper database — Sheets ki limits aa jayengi.
Complex queries honProper database — Sheets me joins nahi hote.
Users badh rahe honServerless + CDN — infrastructure manage mat karo.

6. Common galtiyan — ye mat karna

  • Pehle din se over-engineering karna — users lao, phir infrastructure banao.
  • Bina caching ke Sheets API use karna — rate limit lag jayegi.
  • Sheets ko real database samajhna — iski limits hain (cells, rate limits).
  • Backend migrate karne me der karna — limits aate hi migrate karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: Levels.fyi ne Google Sheets se millions of users kaise handle kiye?

Google Forms se data collect kiya, Sheets ko database ki tarah use kiya, serverless functions se data serve kiya, aur caching se Sheets API ke calls kam kiye. Salary data zyada badalta nahi tha, isliye caching bahut effective thi. Jab limits aayi, tab proper backend banaya.

Q: Start simple ka matlab kya hai?

Pehle simple tools se product banao aur users lao — perfect infrastructure baad me banao. Levels.fyi ne Sheets se shuru kiya, lakhon users aane ke baad backend banaya. Bahut startups ulta karte hain — pehle infrastructure, phir users (jo kabhi aate hi nahi).

Q: Caching ne Levels.fyi ko kaise bachaya?

Salary data zyada badalta nahi tha — isliye ek baar Sheets se data la ke cache me rakh diya, phir lakhon users ko cache se jawab milta tha. Sheets API ko sirf kuch calls per minute jati thi — rate limit nahi lagi, site fast rahi.

8. Quick check

Q1. Levels.fyi ne shuruaat me backend ke liye kya use kiya?

  • PostgreSQL
  • Google Sheets
  • MongoDB

Q2. Sheets API ki rate limit se bachne ke liye kya use kiya?

  • Aur servers
  • Caching
  • Bada database

← PichhlaFixing Bugs Automatically at Meta ScaleAgla →How does Twitter recommend “For You” Timeline in 1.5 seconds?
05Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

How does Twitter recommend “For You” Timeline in 1.5 seconds?

Tum Twitter kholte ho aur 1.5 second me “For You” timeline taiyaar — 50 crore tweets me se sirf tumhare liye chune hue. Ye magic ek 5-stage pipeline hai jo Twitter ne open-source ki thi. Samjho 500 million tweets 1500 candidates tak kaise pahunchte hain.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — Twitter ki ‘For You’ serving pipeline, 5 stages ke saath. Image file ke andar embedded hai.

1. 1.5 second me timeline — sabzi mandi wali kahani

Sabzi mandi me 50,000 thele hain. Tumhe sirf 10 sabzi chahiye. Agar har thele par jaa ke check karo to shaam ho jayegi. Isliye pehle ek banda moti chhant karta hai — kharab aur band thele hata do (500M → 1500). Phir ek expert quality check karta hai — kaun si sabzi fresh aur tumhare taste ki hai. Phir thoda variety mila ke tokri bhar deta hai.

Twitter ka pipeline wahi karta hai: pehle saste filters se 50 crore tweets ko 1500 tak lao, phir bhaari neural network se sirf un 1500 ko rank karo. Bhaari kaam sirf chhote set par — isiliye 1.5 second me ho jata hai.

2. Pipeline ke 5 stages

Twitter ke open-sourced algorithm ke hisaab se — har stage me kya hota hai, aur kitne tweets bachte hain.

Stage 1 — Candidate Sourcing (~500M tweets)

Shuruaat ~500 million tweets se hoti hai. Do sources se candidates aate hain: In-Network — jinko tum follow karte ho, unke tweets; aur Out-of-Network — jinko tum follow nahi karte, lekin tumhare interest se match karte hain (embedding-based retrieval).

Out-of-Network hi “For You” ko interesting banata hai — nahi to tum sirf wahi dekhte jo tum pehle se follow karte ho.

Stage 2 — Global Filtering (→ 1500)

500M se sirf ~1500 candidates bachte hain. Yahan saste, fast rules lagte hain: blocked/muted users ke tweets hatao, tumne pehle dekhe hue hatao, NSFW/spam filter, aur basic eligibility (jaise language, region).

Kyun pehle? Neural network ko 500M tweets par chalana namumkin hai — pehle saste filter se pile ko chhota karo, phir mehenga model chalao. Yehi system design ka golden rule hai: coarse filter pehle, expensive ranking baad me.

Stage 3 — Scoring & Ranking (48M parameter NN)

Ab 48 million parameter wala neural network har candidate ko score deta hai — tum is tweet ko like karoge? Reply karoge? Kitni der dekhoge? Isme hazaaron features hote hain: tumhara past behavior, tweet ki freshness, author se tumhara relation.

Twitter Blue boost: Blue subscribers ke tweets ko ranking me thoda boost milta hai — ye bhi scoring ka ek feature hai. Model ka output ek probability hoti hai, aur usi se tweets sort hote hain.

Interview line: “Ranking model sirf 1500 candidates par chalta hai — isiliye 1.5 second possible hai.”

Stage 4 — Filtering (diversity)

Sirf top score wale tweets dikhaye to timeline ek hi topic se bhar jayegi. Isliye author aur content diversity enforce hoti hai: ek hi author ke zyada tweets nahi, ek hi topic ke zyada tweets nahi.

Is stage me visibility filters bhi lagte hain — jaise tumne kisi author ko mute kiya hai, ya tweet tumhare liye suitable nahi hai. Diversity na ho to user bore ho ke app band kar deta hai.

Stage 5 — Mixing (ads + Who to Follow)

Aakhri stage me ranked tweets me Ads aur “Who to Follow” suggestions mix kiye jate hain. Ads bhi apni alag recommendation pipeline se aate hain — advertiser ki bidding aur tumhare interest ke hisaab se.

Mixing ka balance important hai: zyada ads dikhaye to user pareshan, kam dikhaye to revenue kam. Isliye ad load (kitne % ads) ek tuned parameter hai.

3. Numbers jo interview me kaam aayenge

StageInput → OutputKaam
Candidate Sourcing~500M tweetsIn-network + out-of-network retrieval
Global Filtering500M → 1500Block/mute/spam/duplicate hatao (saste rules)
Scoring & Ranking1500 tweets48M param neural network — like/reply probability
Filtering1500 → ~50-100Author + content diversity
MixingFinal timelineAds + Who to Follow mix karo

Latency budget: poora pipeline ~1.5 second me. Isliye har stage ka time budget fixed hai — ranking model bhi time limit me rehna chahiye, nahi to timeout pe best-effort result dikhaya jata hai. Real systems me deadline hoti hai, perfection nahi.

4. Try karo — ek timeline request ki journey

5. Har stage ka trade-off

StageMehenga ya sasta?Galti ho to kya hoga
Candidate SourcingSasta (retrieval)Achha tweet pool me hi nahi aaya to kabhi dikhega nahi
Global FilteringBahut sasta (rules)Zyada strict ho to timeline khaali; loose ho to spam
Scoring & RankingSabse mehenga (NN)Slow model = timeout = khaali timeline
Diversity FilteringSastaNa ho to ek hi topic/author se feed bhar jayegi
MixingSastaZyada ads = user bhaag jayega; kam ads = revenue kam

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Neural network ko 500M tweets par chalana — pehle saste filters se candidates chhota karo, phir mehenga model.
2. Diversity bhoolna — sirf top-score dikhane se feed ek jaisi ho jati hai aur user bore ho jata hai.
3. Out-of-network candidates ignore karna — sirf followed log dikhaye to ‘For You’ ki koi value nahi.
4. Latency budget na rakhna — ranking perfect ho lekin 10 second lage to user app band kar dega; deadline pe best-effort result do.
5. Ads ko ranking se alag na samajhna — ads ki alag pipeline hoti hai; mixing me balance chahiye.

7. Interview corner

Q: “500M tweets ko 1.5 second me kaise rank karte hain?”
A: Rank nahi karte — pehle candidate sourcing aur global filtering se 1500 tak laate hain, phir neural network sirf un 1500 par chalta hai. Coarse-to-fine pipeline hi latency ka raaz hai.
Q: “In-network aur out-of-network candidates me kya farak hai?”
A: In-network: jinko tum follow karte ho. Out-of-network: embedding similarity se nikale gaye tweets — jinko tum follow nahi karte lekin tumhare interest se match karte hain. ‘For You’ ki discovery yahi se aati hai.
Q: “Diversity filtering kyun zaroori hai?”
A: Sirf score se rank karo to ek hi author ya topic dominate karega. Diversity se feed varied rehti hai aur user zyada der tak scroll karta hai — engagement badhta hai.

8. Quick check

1. Twitter pipeline me neural network kitne candidates par chalta hai?

~1500 candidates par — pehle filtering se 500M chhota kiya jata hai Poore 500 million tweets par Sirf 10 tweets par

2. ‘For You’ me naye logon ke tweets kahan se aate hain?

Out-of-network candidate sourcing — embedding-based retrieval se Sirf ads se Randomly chune jate hain

Ek line me yaad rakh lo: 500M tweets → saste filters se 1500 → neural network se ranking → diversity → ads mix. Bhaari kaam sirf chhote set par hota hai — isiliye poori timeline 1.5 second me ban jati hai.

← PichhlaHow Levelsfyi Scaled to Millions of Users with Google SheetsAgla →How YouTube Handles Massive Video Uploads
06Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

How YouTube Handles Massive Video Uploads

YouTube par har minute 500+ ghante ka video upload hota hai. Har video ko mobile (720p), laptop (1080p) aur TV (4K) ke liye alag-alag format me badalna padta hai — ise transcoding kehte hain. Software se ye slow aur mehenga tha, isliye YouTube ne apna hardware encoder banaya. Dekhte hain kaise.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — YouTube ka hardware encoding (Argos VCU). Image file ke andar embedded hai.

1. Transcoding kya hai? — photo studio wali kahani

Ek photo studio samjho: customer ek badi RAW photo deta hai. Use chahiye: WhatsApp ke liye chhoti, album ke liye badi, aur hoarding ke liye bahut badi. Studio ko ek photo se teen sizes banana padte hain.

YouTube wahi karta hai video ke saath: tum ek video upload karte ho, YouTube use har resolution aur har device ke liye alag-alag version me badalta hai. Yehi transcoding hai — aur har minute 500 ghante video ka matlab hai, ye kaam bahut bada aur lagatar chalta hai.

2. Upload pipeline ke 5 hisse

Guide ke hisaab se — software encoding se hardware encoding tak ka safar.

Upload — har minute 500+ ghante

Creator video upload karta hai — kabhi 100MB, kabhi 10GB. Upload ke waqt video chunks me aata hai, taaki network toote to dobara poora upload na karna pade — sirf bacha hua hissa.

Upload hote hi video object storage me save hota hai, aur transcoding queue me ek job ban jata hai. User ko turant “upload complete” dikh sakta hai, lekin video tab tak process hota rehta hai.

Transcoding — ek video, kai versions

Raw video ko alag-alag resolution (144p se 4K/8K) aur bitrate me badla jata hai. Mobile par slow net ho to 360p, Wi-Fi par 1080p, TV par 4K — player network ke hisaab se version switch karta hai. Ise adaptive bitrate streaming kehte hain.

Har version alag file hoti hai — isliye ek 1GB video ke 6-8 versions mil ke kai GB storage lete hain. Storage ka cost bhi design ka hissa hai.

Software encoding — problem kya thi?

Pehle transcoding CPU par software se hoti thi. COVID me video consumption badha to software encoding slow aur mehenga padne laga — CPU par encode karna ghanton le sakta tha, aur hazaaron CPUs ka bill bahut zyada tha.

Software flexible hota hai (naya codec aaye to update karo), lekin throughput per watt bahut kam hai. Scale par ye model nahi chal sakta tha.

Hardware encoding — YouTube ka Argos VCU

YouTube ne 2021 me apna hardware encoder publish kiya: Argos VCU (Video Coding Unit) — ek special chip jo sirf video encode karne ke liye bani hai. Ek chip hazaaron videos parallel me encode kar sakti hai, CPU se kai guna tez aur kam bijli me.

Trade-off: hardware flexible nahi hota — naya codec aaye to nayi chip chahiye. Lekin YouTube ka volume itna bada hai ki custom hardware ka cost justify hota hai. Chhoti company ke liye software encoding hi sahi hai.

Interview line: “Scale par general-purpose CPU ki jagah special-purpose hardware jeetta hai — throughput per watt aur per dollar dono me.”

Delivery — CDN se tumhare screen tak

Encode hue versions CDN (Content Delivery Network) par distribute hote hain — tumhare sheher ke paas wale server par video pehle se rakha hota hai, taaki play dabate hi video shuru ho.

Player adaptive streaming karta hai: net slow hua to 360p, tez hua to 1080p — bina ruke. Isliye YouTube kabhi “buffer” nahi hota (zyadatar) — quality badalti hai, video nahi rukta.

3. Software vs Hardware encoding

CheezSoftware encoding (CPU)Hardware encoding (Argos VCU)
SpeedSlow — ghante lag sakte hainTez — massive parallel
CostCPU bill bahut zyada scale parChip ka cost, lekin per-video sasta
FlexibilityNaya codec = software updateNaya codec = nayi chip
PowerZyada bijli per videoKam bijli per video
Kiske liye sahiChhoti/medium scaleYouTube jaisi massive scale

Upload ka flow: Upload (chunked) → Object storage → Transcoding queue → VCU encode (saare resolutions) → CDN distribute → Player adaptive streaming. Har step async hai — upload complete dikhne ka matlab video ready hona nahi hota.

4. Try karo — ek video upload karo

5. Pipeline stages — ek table me

StageKya hota haiScale ka challenge
UploadChunked upload, object storage500+ hrs/min — resumable hona chahiye
TranscodingEk video → 6-8 versionsCPU par slow/mehenga → hardware VCU
StorageSaare versions storeEk video kai GB — storage cost bada hai
CDNVersions edge servers parDuniya bhar me copies — invalidation mushkil
PlaybackAdaptive bitrate playerNet badle to quality badle, video na ruke

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Upload ko synchronous samajhna — upload complete ka matlab video ready nahi; transcoding async hoti hai.
2. Ek hi version rakhna — har device aur net speed ke liye alag version chahiye; nahi to mobile par 4K download hoga.
3. Software encoding ko scale par chalana — volume badhe to cost aur time dono explode karte hain; hardware ya managed service dekho.
4. Chunked/resumable upload na banana — 10GB upload beech me toote to user dobara shuru karega aur bhaag jayega.
5. CDN bhoolna — origin server se duniya bhar ko video serve karna slow aur mehenga hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: “YouTube hardware encoder kyun banaya?”
A: Volume: har minute 500+ ghante video. Software (CPU) encoding slow aur mehenga tha — power aur cost per video bahut zyada. Argos VCU chip parallel encode karti hai, tez aur kam bijli me. Scale par custom hardware justify hota hai.
Q: “Adaptive bitrate streaming kya hai?”
A: Ek video ke kai versions (144p–4K) banaye jate hain. Player network speed dekh ke version switch karta hai — net slow ho to quality kam, tez ho to zyada — video ruke bina.
Q: “Resumable upload kyun zaroori hai?”
A: Bade files (GBs) upload karte waqt network toot sakta hai. Chunked upload me sirf bacha hua chunk dobara bhejta hai, poora file nahi — warna user dobara upload nahi karega.

8. Quick check

1. YouTube ne software encoding se hardware encoding ki taraf kyun shift kiya?

Volume itna bada tha ki CPU encoding slow aur mehenga pad raha tha Software encoding kaam nahi karta tha Hardware sasta hota hai hamesha

2. Adaptive bitrate streaming ka matlab kya hai?

Network ke hisaab se video quality (144p–4K) switch hoti hai, video ruke bina Video hamesha 4K me chalta hai Video download karke dekhna padta hai

Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Har minute 500 ghante video: chunked upload, object storage, Argos VCU hardware par parallel transcoding, phir CDN se adaptive streaming. Scale par special hardware jeet ta hai — software har jagah kaafi nahi hota.

Page 62 · System Design 101 · Content ByteByteGo ke guide aur diagram pe based hai, har point ko detail, example aur interview line ke saath Hinglish me expand kiya gaya hai. Diagram image file ke andar embedded hai (62.png q82, 151 KB), isliye bina internet ke bhi dikhegi.

Transcoding ka dimaag — VCU (guide se):
  • Traditional Software Encoding: YouTube ka mission raw video ko alag-alag compression rates me transcode karna hai — mobile (720p), laptop (1080p), high-resolution TV (4K). COVID-19 ke time video consumption bahut badh gaya, to software-based encoding slow aur costly ho gaya — video encoding/decoding ke liye ek specialized processing brain chahiye tha.
  • YouTube’s Transcoding Brain — VCU (Video transCoding Unit): jaise GPU graphics ke liye aur TPU machine learning ke liye bana tha, waise hi YouTube ne VCU banaya warehouse-scale video processing ke liye. Har cluster me kai VCU accelerated servers hote hain; har server me multiple accelerator trays, har tray me multiple VCU cards; har card me encoders, decoders, etc. hote hain.
  • VCU cluster alag-alag resolutions ka video content generate karke cloud storage me store karta hai. Is naye design se previous optimized system ke mukable computing efficiency me 20-33x improvement aaya.
Source:https://github.com/ByteByteGoHq/system-design-101/blob/main/data/guides/how-does-youtube-handle-massive-video-content-upload.md
← PichhlaHow does Twitter recommend “For You” Timeline in 1.5 seconds?Agla →How Does a Typical Push Notification System Work?
07Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

How Does a Typical Push Notification System Work?

Tumhare phone par notification aata hai — “tumhara order nikal gaya!” Ye ek second me kaise pahunchta hai? Peeche ek poora push notification system hai: gateway, distribution service, templates, aur APNS/FCM jaise providers. Is page me uska step-by-step flow samjho.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — ek typical push notification system ka architecture. Image file ke andar embedded hai.

1. Notification system — dakiya wali kahani

Ek gaon me ek dakiya hai. Log use chitthi dete hain (business services), wo unhe sort karta hai — kaun si chitthi kahan jani hai, kis bhasha me hai, kab deni hai — aur phir sahi raste se pahuncha deta hai: koi cycle se, koi bus se, koi hawai jahaz se.

Push notification system wahi dakiya hai: Notification Gateway chitthi leta hai, Distribution Service sort karta hai, Template Repository se sahi format lagata hai, aur provider (APNS/FCM) ke through phone tak pahunchata hai.

2. System ke 5 main hisse

Diagram ke steps ke hisaab se — business service se lekar tumhare phone tak.

Step 1 — Notification Gateway

Business services (order service, payment service) notifications gateway ko bhejte hain. Gateway do mode support karta hai: ek-ek karke (single notification) aur batch me (hazaaron ek saath, jaise sale ki announcement).

Gateway hi entry point hai — authentication, rate limiting aur basic validation yahin hota hai. Bina gateway ke har service seedha provider ko call karegi aur system bikhar jayega.

Step 2 — Distribution Service

Gateway notifications ko distribution service ko deta hai. Yahan message validate hota hai (kya user ne is type ki notification allow ki hai?), format hota hai, aur user ki settings ke hisaab se schedule hota hai (raat 3 baje promo mat bhejo!).

Yehi wo jagah hai jahan user preferences check hoti hain — kisi ne SMS off kiya hai to sirf push jayega, kisi ne sab off kiya hai to kuch nahi jayega.

Template Repository — ek message, kai bhashayein

Notification ka text har baar haath se nahi likha jata — templates hote hain: “Hi {name}, tumhara order {orderId} nikal gaya!” Template me variables bhar ke message banta hai.

Templates se fayda: ek jagah text badlo to saari jagah badal jata hai, aur alag language / channel ke liye alag template — SMS chhota, email lamba, push beech ka.

Step 3 — Providers tak delivery

Aakhir me notification provider ko jata hai: iPhone ke liye APNS (Apple Push Notification Service), Android ke liye FCM (Firebase Cloud Messaging), SMS ke liye SMS gateway, email ke liye email service.

App khud seedha phone ko notification nahi bhej sakta — OS ke through hi jata hai. Isiliye provider ka token (device token) store karna padta hai, aur token expire ho to update karna padta hai.

Sahi tareeka: provider ka response track karo — token invalid ho to use hatao, nahi to tum hamesha dead devices ko notification bhejte rahoge.

Delivery tracking — pahuncha ya nahi?

Notification bhejna kaafi nahi — delivered hua? khola gaya? Ye track karna padta hai. Isse pata chalta hai kaun si notification kaam karti hai aur kaun si spam lagti hai.

Failure pe retry hota hai, lekin limit ke saath — provider down ho to baar-baar retry se provider aur bhi down ho jayega. Aur user ne app uninstall kar di to token invalid milega — use saaf karo.

3. Poora flow — step by step

1. Business service: "Order #123 shipped" → Notification Gateway
   (single ya batch mode)
2. Gateway → Distribution Service
3. Distribution Service:
   - Validate: user ne notification allow ki hai?
   - Format: template se message banao ("Hi Rahul, order nikal gaya!")
   - Schedule: user ki timezone + quiet hours check karo
4. Channel choose karo: Push / Email / SMS / In-App
5. Provider ko bhejo:
   - iOS → APNS, Android → FCM, SMS → SMS gateway
6. Delivery tracking: delivered? opened? token invalid?

Channels: In-App notifications, Email, SMS/OTP, aur Social media pushes — ek hi system se saare channels chalte hain, isliye user ko har jagah consistent message milta hai.

4. Try karo — ek order notification bhejo

5. Channels — ek table me

ChannelKab use karte hainDhyan rakhne wali baat
Push (APNS/FCM)Turant alert — order, OTP, messageDevice token expire hota hai; invalid token saaf karo
In-AppApp khula ho to andar ka alertUser app me hai to push ki zaroorat nahi
EmailDetail wali cheez — bill, receiptSpam folder me na jaye — sender reputation
SMS / OTPCritical — OTP, payment alertMehenga hai; sirf zaroori cheez ke liye
Social media pushEngagement — naya post, likeZyada bhejo to user notification hi band kar dega

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. User ki preference ignore karke sab kuch bhejna — notification band karne ka sabse bada reason spam hai.
2. Raat 3 baje promo bhejna — quiet hours aur timezone check karo, nahi to user app uninstall kar dega.
3. Invalid device tokens kabhi saaf na karna — dead devices ko bhejte rehna provider ka quota aur paise waste karta hai.
4. Retry bina limit ke — provider down ho to retry storm se use aur down kar doge; exponential backoff use karo.
5. Har channel par same message — SMS 160 chars ka hota hai, email lamba; template har channel ke hisaab se banao.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Push notification seedha phone ko kyun nahi bhej sakte?”
A: Kyunki mobile OS (iOS/Android) sirf apne provider (APNS/FCM) se notification accept karta hai. App background me ho to bhi OS hi notification dikhata hai — isliye device token aur provider zaroori hai.
Q: “Batch mode kyun chahiye gateway me?”
A: Sale ya announcement jaise cases me hazaaron notifications ek saath bhejne hote hain. Ek-ek karke bhejna slow hoga; batch mode se throughput milta hai.
Q: “Notification system me user preference kahan check hoti hai?”
A: Distribution service me — validate step par. User ne kaun sa channel on/off kiya hai, quiet hours kya hain — ye sab wahi check hota hai, provider ko bhejne se pehle.

8. Quick check

1. Notification Gateway ke kitne modes hote hain?

Do — single aur batch Sirf ek — single Teen — single, batch aur manual

2. iPhone par push notification kis provider se jata hai?

APNS (Apple Push Notification Service) FCM Seedha app se

Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Business service → Gateway (single/batch) → Distribution Service (validate, format, schedule) → Template → Provider (APNS/FCM/SMS) → phone. User ki preference aur quiet hours sabse upar — notification helpful honi chahiye, spam nahi.

08Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

4 Ways Netflix Uses Caching

Netflix ka goal simple hai: tumhe zyada der tak streaming par rakho. Lekin user ka attention span sirf 90 seconds hai — page slow khula to user bhaag jayega. Isliye Netflix EVCache (distributed key-value store, Memcached par bana) ko 4 alag tareekon se use karta hai.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — Netflix EVCache ke 4 use cases. Image file ke andar embedded hai.

1. 90 seconds — sabzi mandi wali kahani

Ek dukaan me customer aata hai. Agar dukaan wala har cheez ke liye godown tak jaye to customer 90 second me hi nikal jayega. Smart dukaan wala counter par hi sabse zyada bikne wali cheezein rakhta hai — turant de do, customer khush.

EVCache wahi counter hai: jo data baar-baar chahiye, wo memory me rakho; godown (Cassandra/database) tabhi jao jab counter par na ho. Netflix ne is counter ko 4 alag kaam me lagaya hai.

2. EVCache ke 4 use cases

Guide ke hisaab se — har tab me ek use case, kaise kaam karta hai aur kyun.

1. Lookaside Cache — pehle cache, phir DB

App ko data chahiye to pehle EVCache client ko poochta hai. Cache me mila to turant mil gaya (hit). Nahi mila to backend service Cassandra database se laati hai, aur cache ko bhi update kar deti hai taaki agli baar turant mile (miss → fill).

Ye sabse common caching pattern hai — Cache-Aside bhi kehte hain. Application khud cache manage karti hai, isliye control app ke paas rehta hai.

2. Transient Data Store — temporary data

Netflix EVCache ko temporary data rakhne ke liye bhi use karta hai — jaise playback session ki information. Ek service session shuru karti hai, dusri update karti hai, teesri band karti hai.

Ye data permanent nahi hai — session khatam ho to data bhi khatam. Database me likhna iske liye slow aur mehenga hota; cache me rakhna tez aur sahi hai. TTL (time-to-live) laga do, data apne aap expire ho jayega.

3. Primary Store — homepage yahin se banti hai

Netflix har raat pre-compute karta hai — har profile ke liye naya homepage, watch history aur recommendations ke hisaab se. Ye saara data EVCache cluster me likha jata hai, aur online services homepage wahi se padh kar banati hain.

Yahan cache sirf cache nahi, primary store hai — data ka main source hi EVCache hai. Database peeche hai hi nahi is flow me. Isse homepage milliseconds me banti hai.

Sahi tareeka: pre-compute + cache = personalization bina latency ke. User ko pata bhi nahi chalta ki homepage raat ko hi ban gayi thi.

4. High Volume Data — UI strings aur translations

Netflix ke homepage par dikhne wale UI strings aur translations ko bahut zyada baar padha jata hai, aur high availability chahiye. Ek alag process inhe asynchronously compute karke EVCache me publish karta hai.

App wahan se low latency aur high availability ke saath padhti hai. Ye data badalta kam hai, padha bahut zyada jata hai — caching ka perfect case.

3. EVCache kya hai — aur 90-second rule

EVCache = distributed key-value store, Memcached par bana hua
Netflix me 10+ saal se use ho raha hai — most services use karti hain
User ka attention span: ~90 seconds
  → Page 90s me interesting na lage to user chala jayega
  → Har millisecond latency kam karna = user rukega
Lookaside:   cache miss → Cassandra → cache fill
Transient:   playback session — TTL ke saath expire
Primary:     pre-computed homepage — cache hi source hai
High-volume: UI strings — async publish, fast read

Interview line: “Cache sirf speed ke liye nahi hai — Netflix me cache hi primary store bhi hai. Pattern ka naam nahi, use case samjho.”

4. Try karo — ek homepage request

5. 4 use cases — ek table me

Use caseData kaisa haiCache ka role
Lookaside CacheBaar-baar padha jane walaPehle cache, miss ho to DB + fill
Transient Data StoreTemporary — playback sessionSirf cache me, TTL se expire
Primary StorePre-computed homepageCache hi main source hai
High Volume DataUI strings, translationsAsync publish, fast + available read

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Har data ko cache karna — jo data kabhi dobara nahi padha jata, use cache karna memory waste hai.
2. Cache ko primary store samajh ke backup na rakhna — cache evict ho sakta hai; critical data ka durable source hona chahiye.
3. TTL na lagana — transient data hamesha ke liye cache me reh jayega aur memory bhar jayegi.
4. Cache stampede ignore karna — popular key expire hote hi hazaaron requests DB par toot padengi; lock ya pre-warming use karo.
5. Cache invalidation bhoolna — purana data dikhane se user ko galat homepage dikhega; write pe invalidate karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Lookaside cache (cache-aside) kaise kaam karta hai?”
A: App pehle cache dekhti hai. Hit ho to wahi se data. Miss ho to database se laati hai aur cache me bhar deti hai taaki agli baar hit ho. Cache manage karne ki zimmedari application ki hoti hai.
Q: “Netflix EVCache ko primary store ki tarah kyun use karta hai?”
A: Homepage har raat pre-compute hoti hai aur EVCache me likhi jati hai. Online services wahi se padhti hain — isse homepage milliseconds me banti hai, bina database ke. Data recoverable hai (dobara compute ho sakta hai), isliye cache primary ban sakta hai.
Q: “Transient data ke liye database kyun nahi?”
A: Playback session jaisa data temporary hota hai aur bahut baar update hota hai. Database me likhna slow aur mehenga hai; cache me TTL ke saath rakhna tez hai aur data apne aap expire ho jata hai.

8. Quick check

1. Netflix me pre-computed homepage kahan se serve hoti hai?

EVCache se — cache hi primary store hai is flow me Seedha Cassandra se har baar User ke phone se

2. Lookaside cache me miss hone par kya hota hai?

Database se data laa kar cache me bhar diya jata hai User ko error dikhaya jata hai Cache hamesha ke liye band ho jata hai

Ek line me yaad rakh lo: EVCache sirf ek cache nahi — Netflix use lookaside, transient store, primary store aur high-volume data, chaaron tareekon se karta hai. 90-second attention span jeetne ka raaz hai: jo chahiye wo memory me pehle se ho.

← PichhlaHow Does a Typical Push Notification System Work?Agla →0 to 1.5 Billion Guests: Airbnb's Architectural Evolution
09Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

0 to 1.5 Billion Guests: Airbnb's Architectural Evolution

Airbnb aaj 200+ countries me hai, 4 million hosts aur 1.5 billion guests. Lekin shuruaat ek simple Ruby on Rails monolith (Monorail) se hui thi. Hypergrowth ne use toda, aur Airbnb Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) ki taraf badha. Ye evolution samjho.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — Airbnb ki architectural evolution: Monorail se SOA tak. Image file ke andar embedded hai.

1. Monorail se SOA tak — ghar banane wali kahani

Pehle ek chhota sa ghar banao — ek kamra, ek kitchen, sab kuch ek jagah. Jab parivaar badhe to kamre jodo, phir floor jodo, phir alag building. Airbnb ka architecture wahi hai: pehle ek monolith (Monorail) — ek hi application me sab kuch.

Jab guests karodon me ho gaye, to ek hi application me sab kuch rakhna mushkil ho gaya — deploy slow, team ek dusre ke code se takra rahi thi. Tab Airbnb ne SOA apnaya: alag-alag services, gateway ke peeche, har service ka apna kaam.

2. Evolution ke 4 service layers

Monorail ke baad SOA me kaun si services bani — neeche se upar tak.

Monorail — Ruby on Rails monolith

Airbnb ki shuruaat Monorail se hui — ek Ruby on Rails application, single-tier, client aur server dono ka kaam ek hi jagah. Chhoti team ke liye perfect: deploy aasan, code ek jagah, debugging simple.

Problem kab aayi? Hypergrowth me: ek change deploy karne me ghante, ek team ka bug saare system ko rok de, aur code ka ownership confuse — kis hisse ka malik kaun hai, pata nahi.

Data Service — sabse neeche wali parat

SOA ki sabse neeche wali layer: Data Service — data entities par saare read/write operations ka entry point. Jaise listing ka data chahiye to Data Service se hi milega, seedha database se nahi.

Isse fayda: database ka access ek jagah control hota hai — caching, validation aur access rules ek hi jagah lagte hain.

Derived Data Service — halki business logic

Ye services Data Service se padhti hain aur basic business logic lagati hain — jaise listing ka price calculate karna, availability nikalna.

Ye layer isliye hai taaki Data Service saaf rahe (sirf data ka kaam) aur business logic alag rahe. Chhoti logic yahan, badi logic upar.

Middle Tier aur Presentation Service

Middle Tier Service — important business logic jo na Data Service me fit hoti hai na Derived me — jaise booking ka poora flow, payment ke saath coordination.

Presentation Service — sabse upar: saari services se data le kar frontend ke hisaab se aggregate karti hai. Mobile ko chhota response, web ko bada — ye yahin decide hota hai. Client seedha in services ko nahi, gateway ko call karta hai, aur gateway request ko sahi services tak pahunchata hai.

Result: Migration ke baad Monorail khatam — saare reads/writes nayi services me chale gaye.

3. Monolith vs SOA — kab switch karna hai

CheezMonorail (Monolith)SOA (Services)
TeamChhoti team, ek codebaseBadi teams, har service ki apni team
DeployPoora app ek saath deployHar service alag deploy
OwnershipConfusing — kis code ka malik kaun?Clear — har service ka owner hai
FailureEk bug poora app rok deEk service down, baaki chalte hain
ComplexityKam — sab ek jagahZyada — network, gateway, monitoring

Gateway ka kaam: client gateway ko request bhejta hai, gateway use sahi services tak route karta hai. Client ko ye pata nahi hota andar kitni services hain — uske liye ek hi API hai.

4. Try karo — ek booking ki journey

5. SOA ki layers — ek table me

LayerKaamExample
Data ServiceData entities par read/writeListing ka data lao/badal do
Derived Data ServiceData + basic logicPrice aur availability nikalo
Middle Tier ServiceBadi business logicBooking + payment flow
Presentation ServiceFrontend ke hisaab se aggregateMobile ko chhota, web ko bada response
GatewayRouting + entry pointClient ki request sahi service tak

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Pehle din se microservices banana — monolith jab tak dard na de, use mat todo; Airbnb ne bhi Monorail se shuru kiya tha.
2. Migration bina gateway ke — client ko har service ka pata chal jayega; gateway se abstraction rakho.
3. Data Service ke bina seedha DB access — har service seedha database chhooye to data rules bikhar jayenge.
4. Service boundaries galat kaatna — galat jagah todi to services ke beech chatty calls honge aur latency badhegi.
5. Monolith ko ‘galat’ kehna — monolith galat nahi hota; galat time par todna galat hota hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Airbnb ne monolith se SOA me migrate kyun kiya?”
A: Hypergrowth me Monorail slow deploy, confusing ownership aur ek bug se poora system rukne ki problem de raha tha. SOA se har service ki apni team, alag deploy aur clear ownership mila.
Q: “SOA me gateway kyun hota hai?”
A: Client ko andar ki services ki complexity nahi dikhni chahiye. Gateway ek entry point hai — routing, authentication aur aggregation wahi se hota hai.
Q: “Data Service layer ka fayda kya hai?”
A: Database ka access ek jagah control hota hai — caching, validation aur rules ek jagah lagte hain. Har service seedha DB chhooye to rules bikhar jayenge.

8. Quick check

1. Airbnb ka pehla monolith kis naam se jana jata tha?

Monorail — Ruby on Rails par bana tha Airbus Monsoon

2. SOA me sabse upar wali layer kaun si hai?

Presentation Service — frontend ke hisaab se data aggregate karti hai Data Service Database

Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Monorail (monolith) se shuru karo, hypergrowth me dard ho to SOA me jao: Data → Derived → Middle Tier → Presentation, gateway ke peeche. Architecture business ke saath badalta hai, pehle din se nahi.

10Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

How Netflix Scales Push Messaging

Netflix ke 22 crore users hain — iPhone, Android, smart TV, Roku, FireStick, browser — sab par notifications bhejne hain, near real-time me. Ek hi system se itne devices par push kaise? Is page me Netflix ke push messaging ki 7-step journey samjho.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — Netflix ka push messaging system. Image file ke andar embedded hai.

1. Push messaging — school ki ghanti wali kahani

Ek school me ghanti bajti hai — sab classes ek saath sunte hain. Lekin har class ko alag message chahiye: 5th class ko “games period”, 10th ko “exam”. Isliye beech me ek announcement system hai jo decide karta hai kaun si class ko kya sunana hai, aur kaun se speaker se.

Netflix ka push system wahi hai: event aata hai, event management engine decide karta hai kaun se device ko kya bhejna hai, priority queues me daalta hai, aur phir har device type ke liye sahi rasta (FCM, APNs, Zuul Push) chun ta hai.

2. Push notification ki 7-step journey

Guide ke hisaab se — event trigger hone se lekar phone/TV par notification aane tak.

Step 1-2 — Event trigger aur Event Management Engine

Push events teen tareekon se trigger hote hain: clock (naya show release hua), user action (tumne kuch dekha), ya systems (billing ya recommendation engine).

Events event management engine ko jate hain. Ye engine specific events ko sunta hai aur unhe aage forward karta hai — kaun sa event kis queue me jayega, ye priority-based rules se decide hota hai.

Step 3 — Priority-based queues

Saare events ek hi line me nahi lagte — priority ke hisaab se alag queues banti hain. “Tumhara show aa gaya” jaisi important notification pehle, “naya trailer” jaisi baad me.

Kyun zaroori hai? Agar sab ek queue me ho to ek bade campaign (jaise naye season ki announcement) ki wajah se tumhara personal notification ghanton late ho jayega. Priority se important pehle jata hai.

Step 4 — Event priority-based processing cluster

Queues se events processing cluster leta hai, aur har device ke liye push notification data generate karta hai — kya likha hoga, kis language me, kaun si image hogi.

Ye cluster hi personalization karta hai: tum Hindi dekhte ho to Hindi message, tumne horror dekha to horror show ki notification.

Step 5 — Cassandra me store

Notification data Cassandra database me store hota hai — taaki agar delivery fail ho to dobara bhej sakein, aur history track kar sakein (kis user ko kab kya bheja).

Cassandra isliye kyunki writes bahut zyada hain (karodon notifications) aur scale horizontal chahiye — node add karo, capacity badhao.

Step 6-7 — Outbound messaging: FCM, APNs, Zuul Push

Ab notification outbound messaging systems ko jati hai — device ke hisaab se rasta alag hai:

Android → FCM (Firebase Cloud Messaging), Apple devices → APNs, aur Web, TV aur streaming devices → Netflix ka apna Zuul Push. TV aur browser ke liye koi standard provider nahi hota, isliye Netflix ne apna solution banaya.

Interview line: “Har device ka rasta alag hota hai — ek provider se sab kuch nahi hota.”

3. Scale — numbers me

CheezNumber / Detail
Users220 million (22 crore)
Latency requirementNear real-time — notification late ho to bekaar
Supported clientsiOS, Android, smart TVs, Roku, Amazon FireStick, web browser
Android rastaFCM
Apple rastaAPNs
Web / TV rastaZuul Push (Netflix ka apna)
StorageCassandra — notification data + history

Trigger types: clock (scheduled), user actions, aur backend systems — teeno se events aate hain, isliye engine ko har type sunna padta hai.

4. Try karo — ek ‘naya show’ notification

5. Device ke hisaab se rasta

DeviceRastaKyun alag
Android phoneFCMGoogle ka standard provider
iPhone / iPadAPNsApple ka standard provider
Smart TV / Roku / FireStickZuul PushTV ke liye koi standard push provider nahi
Web browserZuul PushBrowser push Netflix khud handle karta hai
SabhiCassandra pehleDelivery fail ho to retry aur history ke liye

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Sab devices ko ek hi provider se bhejna — TV aur web ke liye FCM/APNs nahi hota; har device ka rasta alag hai.
2. Priority queues na banana — ek bade campaign se personal notifications dab jayenge.
3. Notification data store na karna — fail hone par retry nahi kar paoge, aur user ko pata bhi nahi chalega.
4. Personalization skip karna — sabko ek jaisa English message bhejna; language aur taste ke hisaab se message badlo.
5. Near real-time ko ‘best effort’ samajhna — notification ghanton late ho to uski value khatam; latency budget rakho.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Netflix TV aur web ke liye Zuul Push kyun use karta hai?”
A: Kyunki smart TV, Roku aur browser ke liye FCM/APNs jaisa standard provider nahi hota. Isliye Netflix ne apna push solution banaya jo in devices tak notification pahuncha sake.
Q: “Priority-based queues kyun zaroori hain?”
A: Saare events ek queue me honge to ek bada campaign personal notifications ko dabaa dega. Priority se important (jaise tumhara show release) pehle jata hai, general announcement baad me.
Q: “Notification data Cassandra me kyun store karte hain?”
A: Delivery fail ho to retry ke liye, aur history/audit ke liye — kis user ko kab kya bheja. Writes karodon me hain, isliye horizontally scalable Cassandra sahi hai.

8. Quick check

1. Netflix par Android devices ko notification kis se jata hai?

FCM (Firebase Cloud Messaging) APNs Zuul Push

2. Smart TV aur web browser ke liye Netflix kya use karta hai?

Zuul Push — Netflix ka apna solution FCM SMS

Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Event trigger → engine → priority queues → processing cluster → Cassandra → FCM (Android), APNs (Apple), Zuul Push (TV/web). Har device ka rasta alag, priority se important pehle — isiliye 22 crore users ko near real-time notification milti hai.

11Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

How Netflix Really Uses Java

Netflix predominantly Java shop hai — streaming, internal apps, movie production apps — har backend application Java me hai. Lekin unka Java stack static nahi raha: API gateway se lekar BFFs aur reactive programming tak, ye kai iterations se guzra hai. Dekhte hain kaise.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — Netflix Java kaise use karta hai. Image file ke andar embedded hai.

1. Java stack ki kahani — ek sheher ka vikas

Ek sheher pehle ek sadak se shuru hota hai, phir chauraha, phir flyover, phir metro. Netflix ka Java stack bhi aise hi badha: pehle simple Java 8 microservices, phir alag-alag clients ke liye BFF (Backend-for-Frontend), phir Groovy aur RxJava se reactive programming.

Har iteration ek problem ka jawab thi — ek gateway sab clients ke liye kaafi nahi tha, to har client ke liye alag backend bana. Ye page un iterations ko samjhata hai.

2. Java stack ke iterations

Guide ke hisaab se — Netflix ka Java stack kaise badla.

Java har jagah

Netflix predominantly a Java shop hai — streaming apps, internal tools, movie production apps — har backend application Java me hai. Ye consistency hiring, libraries aur tooling ko aasan banati hai.

Java 8 se shuruaat hui — microservices Spring Boot par, har functionality ek microservice ke paas.

API Gateway — ek darwaza

Microservices architecture me har functionality ek microservice ke paas hai. Client seedha hazaaron services ko call nahi karta — beech me API Gateway hai (Zuul), jo requests ko sahi service tak pahunchata hai.

Gateway se auth, rate limiting aur routing ek jagah hota hai. Lekin ek gateway sab clients ke liye kaafi nahi tha — yahi agla problem tha.

BFFs — Backend-for-Frontend

Ek hi gateway se TV, mobile aur browser — teeno ko serve karna mushkil tha, kyunki har client ki zaroorat alag thi. Isliye Netflix ne BFF (Backend-for-Frontend) banaye — har client type ke liye alag backend, jo us client ke hisaab se data aggregate karta hai.

Mobile BFF mobile ko chhota response deta hai, TV BFF TV ko bada. Client ko wahi milta hai jo use chahiye — na zyada, na kam.

Groovy aur RxJava — reactive programming

BFFs me Netflix ne Groovy (JVM par chalne wali dynamic language) aur RxJava (reactive extensions) use kiye. RxJava se kai services ko parallel me call karke result combine kiya ja sakta hai — ek ke baad ek wait nahi karna padta.

Reactive ka matlab: ek request ke liye 5 services chahiye to saari ek saath bulao, jo pehle aaye use karo, sab aa jayein to combine karo. Latency bahut kam ho jati hai.

Interview line: “BFF + reactive = har client ko apna data, sabse kam latency me.”

Aaj — Java stack mature hai

Aaj Netflix ka Java stack mature hai: Spring Boot microservices, Zuul gateway, BFFs, aur reactive patterns. Java versions bhi aage badhe hain — lekin philosophy wahi hai: ek primary language, sahi patterns, aur client ke hisaab se backend.

Lesson: stack ek baar me nahi banta — har iteration ek real problem ka jawab hoti hai. Pehle din se BFF mat banao; jab ek gateway kam pad jaye, tab banao.

3. Ek request — gateway se BFF tak

Mobile app → Zuul (API Gateway)
  → Mobile BFF (Groovy + RxJava)
    → RxJava: 5 services ko PARALLEL call
      → Movie service, User service, Recommendations,
        Playback service, Personalization
    → Results combine → mobile ke hisaab se response
  → App ko JSON milta hai — sirf wahi fields jo chahiye
TV app → TV BFF → wahi services, alag aggregation
Web app → Web BFF → wahi services, alag aggregation

RxJava ka fayda: 5 services ko ek ke baad ek bulao to 5x latency; parallel bulao to sirf sabse slow wale jitni latency. Isiliye BFFs reactive hain.

4. Try karo — mobile se ek movie page kholo

5. Stack ke hisse — ek table me

HissaTechKyun
LanguageJava (8 se aage)Har backend app — consistency
FrameworkSpring BootMicroservices jaldi bante hain
GatewayZuulEk entry point — routing, auth
BFFGroovy + RxJavaHar client ka apna backend, parallel calls
ReactiveRxJavaKai services parallel — latency kam
ServicesMicroservicesHar functionality ka owner alag

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Ek gateway se sab clients serve karna — mobile, TV, web ki zaroorat alag hai; BFF banao jab zaroorat ho.
2. Services ko ek ke baad ek (sequential) call karna — parallel (reactive) se latency kai guna kam hoti hai.
3. Har team ko alag language dena — ek primary language se hiring aur tooling aasan rehti hai.
4. Pehle din se BFF banana — jab tak ek gateway dard na de, BFF over-engineering hai.
5. Java ko ‘purana’ keh ke har cheez nayi language me likhna — Netflix dikhata hai Java scale par kaam karta hai; language se zyada architecture matter karta hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: “BFF (Backend-for-Frontend) kya hai?”
A: Har client type (mobile, TV, web) ke liye alag backend jo us client ke hisaab se data aggregate karta hai. Ek gateway sabko ek jaisa data de to mobile ko zyada data milega aur TV ko kam — BFF se har client ko wahi milta hai jo chahiye.
Q: “RxJava Netflix kyun use karta hai?”
A: BFF ko ek page ke liye kai services call karni hoti hain. RxJava se wo parallel call hoti hain aur results combine hote hain — sequential calls se latency kai guna zyada hoti.
Q: “Netflix predominantly Java shop kyun hai?”
A: Consistency: hiring, libraries, tooling aur debugging — sab ek language me aasan hota hai. Java mature, fast aur scale-proven hai; har problem ke liye nayi language nahi chahiye.

8. Quick check

1. Netflix me har client (mobile/TV/web) ke liye alag backend ko kya kehte hain?

BFF — Backend-for-Frontend CDN Database

2. RxJava ka sabse bada fayda kya hai?

Kai services ko parallel call karke latency kam karna Database ko tez karna App ko sundar banana

Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Netflix Java shop hai: Spring Boot microservices, Zuul gateway, har client ke liye Groovy + RxJava BFF, aur parallel calls se kam latency. Stack ek baar me nahi banta — har iteration ek real problem ka jawab hai.

Groovy aur RxJava wale approach me UI developers ko Groovy scripts likhne ka extra kaam karna padta tha, aur reactive programming aam taur par mushkil hoti hai. Isi liye Netflix agle iteration me GraphQL Federation ki taraf gaya — federation me har service apna GraphQL schema contribute karti hai aur gateway unhe ek unified graph ki tarah jodkar serve karta hai.
