12Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

Evolution of Airbnb’s Microservice Architecture

Airbnb ki microservice journey 3 stages me hui: Monolith (2008–2017), Microservices (2017–2020), aur phir uske baad ka refinement. Ye guide Airbnb ki microservice evolution par ek tech talk par based hai. Samjho har stage me kya problem thi aur kya seekha.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — Airbnb ki microservice evolution, 3 stages. Image file ke andar embedded hai.

1. 3 stages — ek dukaan se mall tak

Pehle ek chhoti dukaan — ek hi malik, sab kuch ek jagah. Phir dukaan badi hui to alag-alag counters — kapde alag, kirana alag. Phir mall — har shop ka apna malik, apna timing, apna staff.

Airbnb bhi aise hi badha: Monolith (ek dukaan) → Microservices (alag counters) → aur phir seekha ki alag counters ka bhi apna dard hai. Har stage ka apna lesson hai.

2. 3 stages — detail me

Guide ke hisaab se — har stage ki dates, problem aur solution.

Stage 1 — Monolith (2008–2017)

Airbnb ek simple marketplace tha — hosts aur guests. Sab kuch ek Ruby on Rails monolith me tha. Chhoti team, tez development, simple deploy.

Challenges: confusing team ownership — kis code ka malik kaun hai, pata nahi; unowned code — koi code aisa jiska koi malik hi nahi; aur slow deployment — ek chhota change bhi poora app deploy karta tha.

Stage 2 — Microservices (2017–2020)

Monolith ki problems solve karne ke liye Airbnb microservices me gaya: key services ko alag kiya — jaise search, booking, payments, messaging — har service ki apni team aur apna deploy.

Fayda: clear ownership, tez deploy, ek service ka bug dusre ko nahi rokta. Naya dard: services ke beech communication, distributed debugging, aur data consistency — ye sab monolith me free milta tha, ab khud manage karna padta hai.

Stage 3 — Microservices ke baad

Microservices ke baad Airbnb ne seekha: har cheez ko microservice mat banao. Service boundaries sahi honi chahiye — galat jagah todi to services ke beech bahut saari chatty calls hongi aur latency badhegi.

Is stage me focus raha: platform tools (service mesh, observability), sahi service boundaries, aur monolith se nikle hue shared code ko saaf karna.

Interview line: “Microservices ka matlab har function alag service nahi — matlab sahi boundaries.”

Team ownership — asli problem

Airbnb ki migration ki sabse badi wajah technical nahi, organizational thi: confusing ownership aur unowned code. Jab team badi hoti hai, to har code ka malik hona chahiye — nahi to bug aane par koi fix nahi karta.

Microservices se har service ka owner clear ho gaya — “ye service meri team ki hai, iska deploy aur on-call hum karte hain.”

Slow deployment — monolith ka dard

Monolith me ek line badlo to poora app deploy karna padta tha — test, build, deploy — ghanton ka kaam. Teams ek dusre ka wait karti thi.

Microservices me har service alag deploy hoti hai — ek team apni service din me kai baar deploy kar sakti hai, dusri team ko roke bina. Yehi velocity ka fark hai.

3. Timeline — ek nazar me

StageTimeKya thaProblem
Monolith2008–2017Ruby on Rails, ek appConfusing ownership, unowned code, slow deploy
Microservices2017–2020Key services alagClear ownership, tez deploy — lekin distributed complexity
Refinement2020 ke baadBoundaries + platformSahi boundaries, observability, service mesh

Based on: ek speaker ki tech talk — Airbnb ki microservice evolution par.

4. Try karo — ek feature ki journey, teeno stages me

5. Monolith vs Microservices

CheezMonolithMicroservices
OwnershipConfusing — code ka malik unclearClear — har service ki team
Deploy speedSlow — poora app ek saathTez — har service alag
FailureEk bug poora app rok deEk service down, baaki chalte hain
ComplexityKam — sab ek jagahZyada — network, tracing, consistency
Best forChhoti team, simple domainBadi team, clear boundaries

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Ownership problem ko technical problem samajhna — Airbnb ki wajah organizational thi; pehle team structure samjho.
2. Har function ko alag microservice banana — galat boundaries se chatty calls aur latency badhegi.
3. Microservices me jaa ke monolith wali soch rakhna — distributed debugging aur tracing ke bina microservices andhere me hain.
4. Slow deployment ko ‘normal’ maan lena — deploy slow hai to velocity kam hai; ye architecture ka signal hai.
5. Migration ek saath karna — strangler fig pattern se dheere-dheere nikalo, big-bang mat karo.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Airbnb ne microservices me migrate kyun kiya?”
A: Monolith me team ownership confusing thi, unowned code tha, aur deployment slow tha. Microservices se har service ka owner clear hua aur deploy tez hua. Wajah organizational thi, sirf technical nahi.
Q: “Microservices ka sabse bada nuksaan kya hai?”
A: Distributed complexity — network calls, debugging, data consistency, aur observability — ye sab monolith me free milta tha. Isliye boundaries sahi honi chahiye.
Q: “Monolith se microservices me kaise migrate karte hain?”
A: Strangler fig pattern: dheere-dheere ek service nikalo, traffic us par shift karo, monolith chhota karte jao. Big-bang migration risky hoti hai.

8. Quick check

1. Airbnb ka monolith period kab tak tha?

2008–2017 — phir microservices (2017–2020) aaye 2008–2010 2020 ke baad bhi monolith hi tha

2. Airbnb ki migration ki sabse badi wajah kya thi?

Confusing team ownership, unowned code aur slow deployment Sirf nayi technology try karni thi Database slow tha

Ek line me yaad rakh lo: 2008–2017 Monolith (Ruby on Rails) → 2017–2020 Microservices → phir refinement. Wajah ownership aur deploy speed thi, sirf technology nahi. Microservices ka fayda sahi boundaries se milta hai — har function alag service nahi hota.

13Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

10 Principles for Building Resilient Payment Systems

Payment system down ho to paise ruk jate hain — aur trust bhi. Shopify ne saalon ke outages se seekh kar 10 principles banaye: timeouts chhote rakho, circuit breaker lagao, capacity gin ke rakho, idempotency keys use karo. Ye principles sirf payment ke nahi — har critical system ke kaam aate hain.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — Shopify ke resilient payment systems ke 10 principles. Image file ke andar embedded hai.

1. Resilient payment system — bijli ka fuse wali kahani

Ghar me bijli ka fuse hota hai: zyada load aaye to fuse udd jata hai, poora ghar jalne se bach jata hai. Payment system me bhi fuse chahiye — ek service slow ho to use turant kaat do, taaki wo poore system ko na le doobe.

Shopify ke 10 principles wahi fuse aur safety net hain: fail fast karo, overload mat hone do, har payment ko dobara safe banao (idempotency), aur jab incident ho to usse seekho. Payment me “retry kar ke dekhte hain” nahi chalta — ek galti se customer ko do baar charge ho sakta hai.

2. 10 principles — 5 tabs me

Guide ke hisaab se Shopify ke 10 principles — har tab me 2 principles.

1. Timeouts chhote rakho — fail fast

Default timeout 60 seconds hota hai — bahut zyada. Shopify ke hisaab se read timeout 5 seconds, write timeout 1 second decent setup hai. Slow service ka 60 second wait karna matlab apne workers ko bandhak banana.

2. Circuit breaker lagao — Shopify ne Semian banaya (Ruby) jo Net::HTTP, MySQL, Redis aur gRPC services ko circuit breaker se protect karta hai. Circuit khula ho to request bhejo hi mat — turant fail karo aur dusra rasta lo.

Interview line: “Timeout + circuit breaker = fail fast. Slow dependency ko tumhare system ko slow karne mat do.”

3. Capacity management — hisaab se lo

Simple maths: queue me 50 requests aayein aur ek request process karne me 100ms lage, to throughput hai 500 requests/second. Capacity ko gin ke rakho — andha scale mat karo.

4. Monitoring aur alerting — Google SRE book ke 4 golden signals: latency, traffic, errors, saturation. Ye chaaro monitor karo — koi ek bhi bigda to alert aana chahiye, customer complain kare usse pehle.

5. Structured logging

Logs ko ek centralized jagah par rakho aur easily searchable banao. Incident ke waqt “log kahan hai?” dhoondhna sabse badi time waste hai.

6. Idempotency keys use karo — payment retry ho to customer ko do baar charge na ho, isliye har payment ke saath ek unique idempotency key bhejo. Shopify ULID (Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier) use karta hai, random UUID v4 ke bajay — ULID sortable hota hai, debugging aasan hoti hai.

7. Reconciliation consistent rakho

Financial partners (banks, payment gateways) ke saath reconciliation breaks (hisab me farak) ko database me store karo aur regularly match karo. Paise ka hisaab kabhi “umeed” par nahi chhodte.

8. Load testing karo — Shopify bade flash sales se pehle regularly load simulate karta hai taaki benchmark pata ho: system kitna load jhel sakta hai, kahan tootega.

9. Incident management

Har incident channel me 3 roles hote hain: IMOC (Incident Manager on Call), SRM (Support Response Manager), aur service owners. Role pehle se clear ho to incident me confusion nahi hoti.

10. Retrospectives — har incident ke baad 3 sawaal: Exactly kya hua? Humne apne systems ke baare me kaun si galat assumptions rakhi thi? Dobara rokne ke liye kya kar sakte hain? Blame nahi, seekhna hai.

3. Numbers jo yaad rakhne hain

PrincipleNumber / ToolYaad rakhne wali baat
TimeoutsRead 5s, Write 1s (default 60s bahut zyada)Fail fast — slow service ka wait mat karo
Circuit breakerSemian (Ruby)Net::HTTP, MySQL, Redis, gRPC protect karo
Capacity50 req × 100ms = 500 rpsThroughput = concurrency / latency
Monitoring4 golden signalsLatency, traffic, errors, saturation
IdempotencyULID (UUID v4 nahi)Sortable key — retry safe + debugging aasan
Incident rolesIMOC, SRM, ownersRole pehle se clear ho
// Idempotency ka idea (pseudo-code)
POST /charge { amount: 100, idempotency_key: "01H..." }
→ Pehli baar: charge karo, key + result store karo
→ Retry same key: naya charge MAT karo, purana result wapas do
// Customer ko do baar charge nahi hoga, chahe retry 10 baar ho

4. Try karo — ek payment ki journey

5. 10 principles — ek table me

PrincipleKya karna haiNa karo to kya hoga
Lower timeoutsRead 5s, Write 1s60s wait se workers atak jayenge
Circuit breakersSemian lagaoSlow service poora system girayegi
Capacity managementThroughput gin ke rakhoOverload se sab kuch slow
Monitoring4 golden signalsProblem pata chalegi customer se
Structured loggingCentralized + searchableIncident me log dhoondhte rahoge
Idempotency keysULID use karoRetry se double charge
ReconciliationBreaks DB me store karoPaise ka hisaab bigad jayega
Load testingFlash sale simulate karoSale ke din system tootega
Incident mgmtIMOC, SRM, ownersIncident me confusion
Retrospectives3 sawaal har incident parWahi galti dobara hogi

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. 60s default timeout rakhna — slow dependency tumhare workers ko kha jayegi.
2. Retry bina idempotency key ke — payment me retry ka matlab double charge ho sakta hai.
3. Circuit breaker na lagana — ek slow service cascading failure laati hai.
4. Load testing sirf sale ke din karna — pehle se simulate karo, benchmark jaano.
5. Incident ke baad blame game — retrospective ka matlab seekhna hai, dosh dena nahi.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Idempotency key kya hai aur payment me kyun zaroori hai?”
A: Ek unique key jo har payment request ke saath jati hai. Network fail hone par client retry karta hai — server key dekh kar samajhta hai ye purani request hai aur dobara charge kiye bina purana result deta hai. Bina iske retry se double charge hoga.
Q: “Circuit breaker kaise kaam karta hai?”
A: Jab koi service baar-baar fail ya slow ho, to breaker circuit khol deta hai — calls us service ko jati hi nahi, turant fail hoti hain. Kuch der baad half-open ho kar ek call try karta hai; success ho to circuit band ho jata hai.
Q: “Timeout 5s/1s kyun — 60s kyun nahi?”
A: Kyunki slow service ka 60 second wait karna matlab tumhare workers/threads 60 second tak bandhak hain. Fail fast karo — 5s me jawab nahi to aage badho, user ko jaldi batao.

8. Quick check

1. Payment retry safe banane ke liye kya use karte hain?

Idempotency key (ULID) — retry par dobara charge nahi hota Bada timeout Retry band kar do

2. Shopify ke hisaab se read aur write timeout kitna decent hai?

Read 5 seconds, Write 1 second Read 60 seconds, Write 60 seconds Read 1 second, Write 5 seconds

Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Fail fast (chhote timeouts), circuit breaker (Semian), capacity gin ke, 4 golden signals monitor karo, ULID idempotency key se retry safe banao, aur har incident se 3 sawaal poochh kar seekho. Payment me galti ki keemat paise me chukani padti hai.

14Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

Evolution of the Netflix API Architecture

Netflix ki API architecture 4 stages se guzri: Monolith → Direct Access → Gateway Aggregation → Federated Gateway (GraphQL). Har stage ek problem ka jawab thi — aur aakhri stage batata hai ki jab developers aur domains badh jayein to API ko kaise manage karte hain.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — Netflix API architecture ke 4 stages. Image file ke andar embedded hai.

1. API evolution — ek restaurant wali kahani

Ek chhota restaurant: ek hi counter, wahi banda order leta hai, khana deta hai, bill karta hai (monolith). Restaurant bada hua to customer seedha kitchen me jaane laga (direct access) — bheed aur confusion. Phir ek waiter aaya jo sab kuch coordinate karta hai (gateway). Phir restaurant chain bani to har branch ka apna menu aur system, lekin customer ko ek hi menu card dikhta hai (federated gateway).

Netflix ki API bhi aise hi badhi — har stage par client aur services ke beech ka rishta badla.

2. 4 stages — detail me

Guide ke hisaab se — har stage me kya tha aur kya problem aayi.

Stage 1 — Monolith

Application ek hi package me deploy hoti hai — jaise ek Java WAR file ya Rails app. Most startups yahin se shuru karte hain — simple, tez, ek jagah sab kuch.

Kab tak theek hai? Jab team chhoti ho aur features kam hon. Jaise hi services badhti hain, monolith bhaari ho jata hai.

Stage 2 — Direct Access

Client app seedha microservices ko call karti hai. Lekin jab microservices sau se hazaaron ho jayein, to un sabko client ke saamne expose karna sahi nahi hai — client ko har service ka pata hona chahiye, aur ek screen ke liye kai calls lagti hain.

Problem: client har service ko jaanta hai — service badli to client bhi badlo. Aur mobile network par 10 calls karna slow hai.

Stage 3 — Gateway Aggregation Layer

Kai use cases me ek screen ke liye kai services chahiye hoti hain — jaise Netflix app ko ek page ke liye movie, production aur talent — 3 APIs chahiye. Gateway aggregation layer ye teeno ko ek call me combine karke deta hai.

Client ko ek hi call karni padti hai, gateway peeche se 3 services ko bulata hai aur result jod kar deta hai. Latency kam, client simple.

Stage 4 — Federated Gateway (GraphQL Federation)

Jaise developers aur domain complexity badhi, aggregation layer banana mushkil ho gaya — har team ko gateway team par depend karna padta tha. GraphQL federation se Netflix ne ek single GraphQL gateway banaya jo baaki saari APIs se data fetch karta hai.

Har domain team apna subgraph maintain karti hai, aur federation unhe ek hi graph me jod deta hai. Client ko ek hi GraphQL endpoint dikhta hai, peeche har team independent hai.

Interview line: “Federation ka matlab: ek graph, kai owners — client ko ek API, teams ko independence.”

3. Ek screen ke liye kitni calls?

StageClient kitni calls karta haiProblem
Monolith1 (ek app)Scale nahi hota, deploy slow
Direct Access3+ (har service ko alag)Client ko sab services ka pata; mobile par slow
Gateway Aggregation1 (gateway combine karta hai)Gateway team bottleneck ban jati hai
Federated Gateway1 (GraphQL)Har team apna subgraph maintain karti hai

Example: Netflix home page ko movie + production + talent chahiye. Direct access me 3 calls, gateway me 1 call — gateway peeche se 3 services ko parallel bulata hai.

4. Try karo — ek home page request, 4 stages me

5. Stages — ek table me

StageKya hota haiKab sahi
MonolithEk package — WAR/Rails appStartup, chhoti team
Direct AccessClient seedha services koServices kam hon tab
Gateway AggregationGateway kai services combine kareEk screen ko kai services chahiye hon
Federated GatewayGraphQL federation — ek graph, kai ownersDevelopers aur domains bahut badh jayein

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Sau microservices ko client ke saamne expose karna — client ko har service ka pata chal jayega.
2. Har screen ke liye client se 10 calls karwana — mobile network par slow; gateway se aggregate karo.
3. Aggregation layer ko ek team ka bottleneck banana — federation se har team apna subgraph maintain kare.
4. GraphQL ko ‘sirf query language’ samajhna — federation ke saath ye poora API architecture hai.
5. Monolith ko stage 1 me hi galat kehna — har startup monolith se shuru karta hai, aur sahi bhi hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Gateway aggregation layer kyun chahiye?”
A: Kyunki ek screen ke liye kai microservices chahiye hote hain. Client har service ko alag call kare to slow aur complex ho jata hai. Gateway ek call me saare services se data le kar combine kar deta hai.
Q: “GraphQL federation kya solve karta hai?”
A: Jab developers aur domains badh jayein, to ek central aggregation team bottleneck ban jati hai. Federation me har domain team apna subgraph maintain karti hai, aur ek gateway unhe ek graph me jod deta hai — client ko ek API dikhti hai.
Q: “Direct access kab problem banta hai?”
A: Jab microservices sau se hazaaron ho jayein. Client ko har service ka address, contract aur failure handle karna padta hai — aur mobile par kai calls slow hoti hain.

8. Quick check

1. Netflix ki API architecture ka aakhri (4th) stage kaun sa hai?

Federated Gateway — GraphQL federation Direct Access Monolith

2. Gateway aggregation layer ka kaam kya hai?

Ek client call ke liye kai services se data le kar combine karna Database ko tez karna Client ko seedha database se jodna

Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Monolith → Direct Access → Gateway Aggregation → Federated Gateway (GraphQL). Har stage ek problem ka jawab: pehle simplicity, phir client complexity, phir aggregation bottleneck, phir federation se har team independent.

15Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

How Discord Stores Trillions of Messages

Discord par trillions (lakhon crore) messages store hain. Ye journey 3 databases se hui: MongoDB → Cassandra → ScyllaDB. Har switch ek problem ka jawab tha — RAM khatam, latency unpredictable, maintenance mehenga. Ye page us migration ki kahani hai.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — Discord ka message storage evolution: MongoDB → Cassandra → ScyllaDB. Image file ke andar embedded hai.

1. Discord ki kahani — godown badalne wali kahani

Ek dukaan pehle chhote godown me thi. Saaman badha to godown chhota pad gaya — naya godown liya. Phir saaman itna badha ki godown ka kiraya aur maintenance hi sabse bada kharcha ban gaya — to aisa godown liya jo sasta aur tez ho.

Discord ne bhi 3 godown badle: MongoDB (shuruaat), Cassandra (scale), ScyllaDB (cost + latency). Har switch par data migrate karna pada — bina service roke.

2. 3 databases — 3 stages

Guide ke hisaab se — dates aur numbers ke saath.

Stage 1 — MongoDB (2015)

Discord ka pehla version ek single MongoDB replica par bana tha. Shuruaat me kaafi tha — lekin Nov 2015 tak MongoDB me 100 million messages ho gaye aur RAM data aur index hold nahi kar pa raha tha.

Problem: latency unpredictable ho gayi — kabhi tez, kabhi bahut slow. Message storage ko dusre database par le jana pada.

Stage 2 — Cassandra (2017)

Cassandra chuna gaya — distributed, write-heavy workload ke liye bana hai. 2017 me 12 Cassandra nodes the aur billions messages store the.

Phir scale badhta gaya: 2022 ki shuruaat me 177 nodes aur trillions messages. Lekin ab nayi problem: latency phir unpredictable, aur maintenance operations bahut mehenge ho gaye — repair, compaction, node add karna — sab bhaari.

Stage 3 — ScyllaDB (2022)

Discord ScyllaDB par gaya — Cassandra-compatible database, lekin C++ me likha hai (JVM ke bajay), isliye kam nodes par zyada throughput aur predictable latency.

Fayda: kam nodes = kam cost + kam maintenance. Cassandra se ScyllaDB migration aasan bhi tha kyunki dono ka data model same hai — Cassandra-compatible hone ka yehi fayda hai.

Interview line: “Database switch karna sirf performance ka sawaal nahi — maintenance cost aur operational burden bhi decide karta hai.”

Migration — bina service roke

Trillions messages migrate karna — bina Discord band kiye — sabse mushkil kaam tha. Strategy: dual-write (naye writes dono DB me), phir purana data backfill karo, phir reads naye DB par shift karo, phir purana band karo.

Is dauran consistency ka dhyan rakhna padta hai — ek message do jagah alag na ho. Isiliye migration hafton/mahinon chalti hai, ek din me nahi hoti.

Har switch ki wajah

MongoDB → Cassandra: RAM khatam, 100M messages par latency unpredictable. Cassandra → ScyllaDB: 177 nodes par maintenance mehenga aur latency phir unpredictable.

Lesson: koi database hamesha ke liye sahi nahi hota. Scale badle to database bhi badalna padta hai — aur jo database aaj best hai, wo 5 saal baad bottleneck ban sakta hai.

3. Timeline — numbers me

StageTimeScaleProblem
MongoDB2015100M messages, single replicaRAM khatam — data + index hold nahi hua
Cassandra201712 nodes, billions messagesKaam kiya, lekin scale badha
Cassandra2022 start177 nodes, trillions messagesLatency unpredictable, maintenance mehenga
ScyllaDB2022Trillions messages, kam nodesCassandra-compatible, tez + sasta

Message storage ki khaasiyat: messages kabhi update nahi hote (append-only), aur reads recent messages ki hoti hain — isliye time-based partitioning aur TTL jaisi techniques kaam aati hain.

4. Try karo — ek message store karo, 3 stages me

5. 3 databases — ek table me

DatabaseKabKyun chhoda / chuna
MongoDB2015, 100M msgsRAM khatam — index hold nahi hua
Cassandra2017, 12 nodesDistributed writes ke liye chuna
Cassandra2022, 177 nodesMaintenance mehenga, latency unpredictable
ScyllaDB2022, trillions msgsCassandra-compatible, tez + kam nodes

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Pehle database ko hamesha ke liye sahi maan lena — scale badle to database badalna normal hai.
2. Migration big-bang karna — dual-write + backfill se dheere-dheere shift karo, bina downtime ke.
3. Write-heavy workload ko RAM-based store par rakhna — messages append-only hote hain, disk-based distributed store chahiye.
4. Node count badha ke har problem solve karna — 177 nodes par maintenance hi sabse bada kharcha ban gaya.
5. Cassandra-compatible hone ka fayda na samajhna — ScyllaDB switch aasan tha kyunki data model same tha.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Discord ne MongoDB kyun chhoda?”
A: Nov 2015 tak 100 million messages ho gaye aur MongoDB ki RAM data aur index hold nahi kar pa rahi thi — latency unpredictable ho gayi. Isliye distributed store (Cassandra) ki taraf gaye.
Q: “Cassandra se ScyllaDB kyun gaye?”
A: 2022 me 177 nodes aur trillions messages par Cassandra ki latency unpredictable ho gayi aur maintenance operations bahut mehenge ho gaye. ScyllaDB Cassandra-compatible hai, C++ me hai — kam nodes par zyada throughput aur predictable latency.
Q: “Bina downtime ke database kaise migrate karte hain?”
A: Dual-write: naye writes dono databases me jate hain. Phir purana data backfill karte hain. Phir reads naye DB par shift karte hain. Jab sab verify ho jaye, tab purana DB band karte hain. Ye hafton chal sakta hai.

8. Quick check

1. Discord ne 2015 me MongoDB kyun chhoda?

100M messages par RAM data aur index hold nahi kar pa rahi thi — latency unpredictable ho gayi MongoDB band ho gaya tha MongoDB me messages store nahi hote

2. ScyllaDB switch aasan kyun tha?

Ye Cassandra-compatible hai — data model same hai Isme koi migration nahi chahiye thi Ye free hai

Ek line me yaad rakh lo: MongoDB (100M msgs, RAM khatam) → Cassandra (12 → 177 nodes, trillions msgs, maintenance mehenga) → ScyllaDB (Cassandra-compatible, tez + sasta). Scale badle to database badlo — dual-write + backfill se, bina downtime ke.

ScyllaDB vs Cassandra — p99 latency (guide se):
  • p99 read latency: ScyllaDB me 15ms, Cassandra me 40-125ms.
  • p99 write latency: ScyllaDB me 5ms, Cassandra me 5-70ms.
  • ScyllaDB Cassandra-compatible database hai jo C++ me likhi gayi hai. Discord ne architecture redesign kiya: monolithic API + Rust me likha data service + ScyllaDB-based storage.

16Real-World Case Studies (Part 1)

Evolution of Uber's API Layer

Uber ki API layer 3 generations se guzri: pehle organic (dispatch + API), phir all-encompassing gateway (2200+ microservices), phir self-service, decentralized, layered. Har generation ek nayi problem ka jawab thi — khaas taur par jab Uber sirf rides se nikal kar Freight, Eats aur naye businesses me gaya.

ByteByteGo ka original diagram — Uber ki API layer ki evolution, 3 generations. Image file ke andar embedded hai.

1. 3 generations — ek dukaan se mall tak

Pehle ek dukaan — do counters: ek ride deta hai (dispatch), ek hisaab rakhta hai (API). Phir mall bana — ek hi main gate se sab andar jate hain (gateway). Phir mall itna bada ho gaya ki har shop ka apna gate aur apna system chahiye — lekin mall ka rule sab par lagu ho (decentralized + layered).

Uber ki API layer bhi aise hi badhi — aur har generation me microservices ki ginti badhti gayi.

2. 3 generations — detail me

Guide ke hisaab se — har generation ki dates aur problem.

Gen 1 — Organic evolution (2014)

2014 me Uber ki architecture me do key services thi: dispatch service — rider ko driver se jodti hai; aur API service — users aur trips ka long-term data store karti hai.

Simple thi — lekin jaise hi products badhe, do services kaafi nahi rahi. Har naya feature inhi do services me ghusne laga.

Gen 2 — All-encompassing gateway

Uber ne bahut jaldi microservice architecture adopt kar li. 2019 tak 2,200+ microservices the — aur sabke upar ek all-encompassing gateway tha, jo saari requests ko handle karta tha.

Problem: gateway bahut bada ho gaya — har feature ka logic gateway me, har team gateway team par depend. Gateway hi bottleneck ban gaya.

Gen 3 — Self-service, decentralized, layered

2018 ki shuruaat tak Uber ke completely naye business lines aa gaye: Freight, ATG (self-driving), Elevate, grocery — aur kai naye applications. Ek gateway se sab sambhalna namumkin tha.

Isliye teesri generation: self-service (har team khud apni API manage kare), decentralized (ek central gateway nahi), aur layered (har layer ka apna kaam). Har business line ki apni API layer, shared standards ke saath.

Interview line: “Central gateway tab tak theek hai jab tak ek business ho — naye business aate hi decentralize karna padta hai.”

2200+ microservices — kaise manage karein?

2019 tak 2200+ microservices the. Itni services ko manage karne ke liye chahiye: service discovery (kaun kahan hai), standard contracts (Thrift API definition), aur platform tools (gateway, observability).

Bina standards ke 2200 services ka matlab hai 2200 alag tareeke — isliye Uber ne API definition (Thrift) aur gateway standards banaye.

Layered — har layer ka apna kaam

Layered architecture me har layer ka apna kaam hota hai: edge layer (auth, rate limiting), business layer (domain logic), aur data layer. Har layer independent badal sakti hai.

Isse fayda: ek business line (jaise Freight) apni layer badal sakti hai, dusri (jaise Eats) ko farak nahi padta — lekin shared standards (security, observability) sab par lagu hote hain.

3. Timeline — ek nazar me

GenerationTimeKya thaProblem
Gen 1 — Organic2014Dispatch + API serviceDo services se zyada products nahi sambhalte
Gen 2 — Gateway2019 tak2200+ microservices, ek bada gatewayGateway bottleneck ban gaya
Gen 3 — Decentralized2018 seSelf-service, layered, har business ki apni APIFreight, ATG, Elevate, grocery — sab alag needs

4. Try karo — ek request, 3 generations me

5. 3 generations — ek table me

GenerationStructureBest for
Gen 1 — OrganicDispatch + APIEk product, chhoti team
Gen 2 — GatewayEk bada gateway, 2200+ servicesKai products, ek business
Gen 3 — DecentralizedSelf-service, layeredKai business lines (Freight, Eats, ATG)

6. Common galtiyan — ye 5 mat karna

1. Ek gateway ko hamesha ke liye solution samajhna — business badhe to gateway bottleneck ban jata hai.
2. 2200 services bina standards ke banana — Thrift jaise contracts ke bina har service alag bolti hai.
3. Har business line ko ek hi API me ghusana — Freight aur Rides ki needs alag hain.
4. Decentralize kar ke standards bhoolna — self-service ka matlab ‘jo chahe karo’ nahi; shared security aur observability chahiye.
5. API layer ko ‘sirf routing’ samajhna — ye auth, rate limiting, versioning aur contracts ka ghar hai.

7. Interview corner

Q: “Uber ki API layer 3 generations se kyun guzri?”
A: Pehle 2 services kaafi thi (2014). Phir 2200+ microservices ho gaye aur ek gateway bottleneck ban gaya. Phir naye business lines (Freight, ATG, Elevate) aaye — to self-service, decentralized, layered architecture chahiye thi.
Q: “All-encompassing gateway ka problem kya tha?”
A: Har feature ka logic gateway me aa gaya aur har team gateway team par depend karne lagi. Gateway badlaav ka bottleneck ban gaya — isliye decentralize karna pada.
Q: “Self-service API layer ka matlab kya hai?”
A: Har team khud apni API manage karti hai — gateway team ka wait nahi karti. Lekin shared standards (auth, observability, contracts) sab par lagu hote hain.

8. Quick check

1. 2019 tak Uber ke kitne microservices the?

2,200+ microservices 22 microservices 220 microservices

2. Uber ki teesri generation kya hai?

Self-service, decentralized aur layered API layer Ek aur bada gateway Monolith me wapas

Ek line me yaad rakh lo: Gen 1: dispatch + API (2014) → Gen 2: ek bada gateway, 2200+ microservices (2019) → Gen 3: self-service, decentralized, layered (Freight, ATG, Elevate ke liye). Business badhe to API layer bhi badalni padti hai.

Interactive Labs

4 labs — mushkil concepts ko haath se aazmao. Har lab ka output yahin live dikhta hai.

LABFigma Scaling Stepper — kaunsa step, kab?

Figma ke 3 scaling steps yaad karo: Step 1 vertical scaling + replication, Step 2 vertical partitioning, Step 3 sharding. Neeche users aur table size daalo — lab batayega kaunsa step lagta hai aur kyun.

LABNetflix Caching Chooser — kaunsa data, kaunsa tareeka?

Netflix caching ke 4 tareeke use karta hai: Lookaside Cache, Transient Data Store, Primary Store, High Volume Data. Neeche data type chuno — lab batayega kaunsa tareeka lagta hai aur kyun.

LABPush Notification Flow Simulator — gateway se device tak

Push notification ke 5 steps hain: Notification Gateway → Distribution Service → Template Repository → Providers (FCM/APNs) → Delivery tracking. Devices ki ginti daalo aur flow chalao — har step pe computed numbers dikhenge.

LABPayment Resilience Chooser — failure aaye to kaunsa principle bachayega?

Shopify ke 10 resilient-payment principles me se sahi principle chuno. Neeche failure scenario chuno — lab batayega kaunsa principle lagta hai aur bina uske kya hota.

Interview FAQs

12 FAQs — aaj ke era ke interviews me poochhe jaane wale sawaal, seedhe jawab ke saath. Sawaal par tap karo, jawab khulega.

01Figma ne apne Postgres database ko 100x kaise scale kiya?
Figma ne 3 steps me scale kiya. Step 1 — Vertical Scaling + Replication: sabse bade instance (r5.12xlarge se r5.24xlarge) pe upgrade, 3 read replicas, aur PgBouncer connection pooler. Step 2 — Vertical Partitioning: Figma Files aur Organizations jaise high-traffic tables ko alag-alag databases me daala, har DB ke liye alag PgBouncer. Step 3 — Sharding: jab tables kai TB aur billions of rows ke ho gaye to table ko 10 shards me baanta (user ID se) aur routing ke liye DBProxy banaya. Result: 100X growth handle ho gaya.
02Discord ne MongoDB se Cassandra, phir ScyllaDB kyun migrate kiya?
Discord 2015 me single MongoDB replica par shuru hua; Nov 2015 me 100 million messages par RAM me data + index nahi sama rahe the aur latency unpredictable ho gayi. 2017 me Cassandra par gaye — 12 nodes, billions of messages. 2022 ke start me 177 nodes aur trillions of messages par Cassandra ki latency unpredictable ho gayi aur maintenance (jaise SSTable compaction) bahut mehnga ho gaya. ScyllaDB (Cassandra-compatible, C++ me likhi) par jaane se p99 read latency 15ms ho gayi (Cassandra me 40-125ms) aur p99 write latency 5ms (Cassandra me 5-70ms).
03Twitter "For You" timeline 1.5 seconds me kaise recommend karta hai?
Twitter 5 stages me kaam karta hai. Stage 1 — Candidate Sourcing: ~500M tweets me se candidates nikaale jate hain. Stage 2 — Global Filtering: candidates ko ~1500 tak filter kiya jata hai. Stage 3 — Scoring & Ranking: 48M parameter neural network har tweet ko score karta hai. Stage 4 — Filtering: diversity ke liye filter lagta hai taaki ek hi type ke tweets na dikhein. Stage 5 — Mixing: ads aur Who to Follow suggestions mila kar final timeline banti hai. Poora pipeline 1.5 seconds ke andar chalta hai.
04YouTube har minute 500+ hours ke video uploads kaise handle karta hai?
YouTube ne software encoding se aage badhkar VCU (Video transCoding Unit) banaya — ek specialized hardware accelerator, jaise GPU graphics ke liye aur TPU machine learning ke liye bana tha. Har cluster me kai VCU accelerated servers hote hain, har server me multiple trays aur har tray me multiple VCU cards (encoders, decoders). VCU cluster alag-alag resolutions (720p, 1080p, 4K) ka content generate karke cloud storage me store karta hai. Is design se previous optimized system ke mukable computing efficiency me 20-33x improvement aaya.
05Netflix millions of devices par push messaging kaise scale karta hai?
Netflix ka push system events par chalta hai: event trigger hota hai, Event Management Engine use process karta hai, priority-based queues me daala jata hai (important notifications pehle), priority-based processing cluster use bhejta hai, state Cassandra me store hoti hai, aur outbound messaging FCM (Android), APNs (iOS) aur Zuul Push ke through hoti hai. 220 million users aur near real-time delivery ke liye priority queues aur sharded processing zaroori hain — har notification ko same priority nahi milti.
06Netflix caching ke 4 tareeke kaunse hain aur kab kaunsa use hota hai?
1. Lookaside Cache (Cache-Aside): app pehle cache dekhti hai, miss par DB se laakar cache me daalti hai — jab data DB me rehta hai aur baar-baar padha jata hai. 2. Transient Data Store: temporary data jaise user session seedha cache me — DB tak jaane ki zaroorat nahi. 3. Primary Store: homepage jaise personalized rows seedha cache se bante hain — cache hi primary store hai. 4. High Volume Data: UI strings aur translations jaise chhote, rarely badalne wale data ke liye. Rule: cache lagane se pehle hamesha poochho — data kitni der valid hai aur stale data se kya nuksaan hoga?
07Airbnb monolith se microservices, phir micro + macroservices kyun gaya?
Monolith (2008-2017, Ruby on Rails) me problems the: confusing team ownership + unowned code aur slow deployment. Microservices (2017-2020) ne ye solve kiya — har service ki ek owning team (data fetching, business logic, write workflow, UI aggregation). Lekin hundreds of services aur dependencies humans ke liye manage karna mushkil ho gaya. Isi liye 2020 se Airbnb micro + macroservices hybrid model par kaam kar raha hai, jiska focus APIs ki unification par hai.
08Uber ki API layer 2200+ microservices ke saath kaise evolve hui?
Uber ki API layer 3 generations se guzri. Gen 1 (2014) — Organic evolution: services jaise-jaise badhe, API layer bhi organically badhi. Gen 2 — All-encompassing gateway: ek bada gateway sab kuch handle karne laga, jo bottleneck ban gaya. Gen 3 — Self-service, decentralized, layered: har layer ka apna kaam, teams apni APIs khud manage karti hain. 2200+ microservices ko manage karne ke liye layered design zaroori hai — ek hi gateway sab kuch nahi sambhal sakta.
09Push notification system ke main components kaunse hain?
Ek typical push notification system me 5 main parts hote hain: 1. Notification Gateway — events receive aur validate karta hai. 2. Distribution Service — events ko batches me baantkar sahi channel ki taraf bhejta hai. 3. Template Repository — ek template se har user ke liye personalized message banta hai (bhasha, naam). 4. Providers — FCM (Android), APNs (iOS), SMTP (email), SMS gateways tak delivery. 5. Delivery tracking — kaunsa message pahuncha, kaunsa fail hua, failed wale retry queue me jate hain. Channels: in-app, email, SMS/OTP aur social media pushes.
10Shopify ke resilient payment systems ke 10 principles me sabse important kaunse hain?
10 principles hain: 1. Timeouts chhote rakho (fail fast), 2. Circuit Breaker, 3. Capacity management, 4. Monitoring, 5. Structured logging, 6. Idempotency, 7. Reconciliation consistent rakho, 8. Load Testing, 9. Incident management, 10. Retrospectives. Interview me 3 sabse zyada poochhe jate hain: Idempotency (duplicate charge rokti hai — har request ke saath unique key), Circuit Breaker (slow service ko poora system girane se rokta hai), aur Reconciliation (ledger aur gateway ke records milakar farak pakadta hai). Paise ke mamle me ek bhi duplicate charge mehenga padta hai.
11Meta ka SapFix bugs ko automatically kaise fix karta hai?
SapFix Meta ka tool hai jo bugs ko automatically detect karke fix generate karta hai. Flow: developer Phabricator par change submit karta hai → SapFix Sapienz se test cases chunta hai aur diff par chalata hai → crash detect hone par 4 tarah ke fixes try karta hai (template, mutation, full revert, partial revert) → patched builds par tests chalakar candidate patch chunta hai → human reviewer (wahi developer jisne change kiya tha) ko Phabricator par bhejta hai. 90-day pilot me 57 crashes ke liye 165 patches bane aur fault detection se fix approval tak ka median time sirf 69 minutes tha.
12Levelsfyi ne Google Sheets se millions of users kaise scale kiye?
Levelsfyi 4 steps me scale hua. Step 1: Google Forms + Sheets se shuruaat — zero backend, data seedha sheet me. Step 2: Sheets ko database ki tarah use karna — reads/writes sheet se. Step 3: Serverless + Caching se scale — sheet ke aage cache aur serverless functions laga kar load sambhala. Step 4: jab zaroorat padi, tab proper backend banaya. Seekh: shuruaat me over-engineering mat karo — jab tak traffic chhota hai, simple tools kaafi hain; scale tab karo jab data aur users dono badh jayein.
